title.zh: 卷五十四 列傳第二十四 陸機 陸雲
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第二十四 陸機 陸雲 Volume 54 Biographies 24: Lu Ji

sentences.zh: 陸機，字士衡，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ji, courtesy name Shiheng, was a man of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji, whose courtesy name was Shiheng, came from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖遜，吳丞相。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was Chancellor of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather, Lu Xun, had served as chancellor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父抗，吳大司馬。

translations.literal: His father Kang was Grand Marshal of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Lu Kang, had held the post of grand marshal of Wu.

sentences.zh: 機身長七尺，其聲如鐘。

translations.literal: Ji was seven chi in height; his voice was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji stood seven chi tall, and his voice rang like a bell.

sentences.zh: 少有異才，文章冠世，伏膺儒術，非禮不動。

translations.literal: In youth he had extraordinary talent; his literary writing crowned the age; he embraced Confucian learning and would not act contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he showed rare gifts; his prose outshone his contemporaries. He devoted himself to Confucian teaching and never stepped outside what ritual allowed.

sentences.zh: 抗卒，領父兵為牙門將。

translations.literal: When Kang died, he took his father's troops and became a Ya-men general.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Kang died, he inherited his father's command and was appointed a garrison general.

sentences.zh: 年二十而吳滅，退居舊裏，閉門勤學，積有十年。

translations.literal: At age twenty Wu was destroyed; he withdrew to his old home, closed his doors and studied diligently, for ten years in accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty when Wu fell. He retired to his ancestral district, shut his gate, and studied without stint for a full decade.

sentences.zh: 以孫氏在吳，而祖父世為將相，有大勳于江表，深慨孫皓舉而棄之，乃論權所以得，皓所以亡，又欲述其祖父功業，遂作《辯亡論》二篇。

translations.literal: Because the Sun house was in Wu, and his grandfather and father for generations were generals and ministers, with great merit south of the Yangzi, he deeply lamented that Sun Hao had raised it and cast it away; he therefore discussed why Quan had gained and why Hao had perished, and also wished to narrate his grandfather's and father's accomplishments, and so composed two essays titled Discourse on [Wu]'s Demise.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun clan had ruled Wu, and his grandfather and father had for generations held the highest civil and military posts, earning great distinction south of the Yangzi. He grieved that Sun Hao had inherited that legacy only to throw it away. He set out how Sun Quan had succeeded and Sun Hao had failed, and he wished to commemorate his forebears' achievements, so he wrote two essays, the Discourses on the Fall of Wu.

sentences.zh: 其上篇曰：

translations.literal: The upper piece says:
translations.idiomatic: The first essay begins:

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏失禦，奸臣竊命，禍基京畿，毒遍宇內，皇綱弛頓，王室遂卑。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han lost the reins; crafty ministers seized the mandate; disaster took root in the capital region; poison spread through the realm; the imperial net slackened and fell; the royal house became base.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Han lost its grip: favorites stole power, calamity fastened on the capital, and poison seeped across the empire until the dynastic order frayed and the throne itself sank low.

sentences.zh: 於是群雄蜂駭，義兵四合。

translations.literal: Then the heroes swarmed like startled bees, and righteous armies converged from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Then rival warlords rose on every side, and armies gathered in the name of righteousness from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 吳武烈皇帝慷慨下國，電發荊南，權略紛紜，忠勇伯世，威棱則夷羿震盪，兵交則醜虜授馘，遂掃清宗祊，蒸禋皇祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu Lie of Wu stirred passionately in the lower lands; like lightning he rose from south of Jing; stratagems crowded the age; loyalty and courage rivaled the world; his awe struck down the barbarian archers; in battle the ugly captives offered severed heads; thus he swept clean the ancestral shrine and offered thick sacrifice to the august ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu Lie of Wu roused the south: he shot forth from Jing like lightning, schemes thick upon schemes, loyalty and courage unmatched. His majesty laid low the strongest bowmen; wherever blades crossed, the foe surrendered heads. He cleared the temple of the Sun ancestors and heaped the sacrifices before their spirits.

sentences.zh: 于時雲興之將帶州，猋起之師跨邑，哮闞之群風驅，熊羆之族霧合。

translations.literal: At that time cloud-rising generals girded provinces; gale-rising armies spanned districts; roaring packs were wind-driven; bearlike clans gathered like fog.
translations.idiomatic: Generals sprang up like clouds, each claiming a province; hosts rose like squalls and overran town after town; howling warbands swept along like driven wind; picked fighters massed as thick as mist.

sentences.zh: 雖兵以義動，同盟戮力，然皆苞藏禍心，阻兵怙亂，或師無謀律，喪威稔寇。

translations.literal: Although the armies moved under the banner of righteousness and the alliance joined strength, yet all harbored treacherous hearts, relied on arms and clung to disorder, or had armies without planning or discipline, lost awe and nourished bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Though they marched under the cause of justice and swore common effort, most nursed private ambition, clung to arms and fed on chaos, or led troops without plan or discipline—so awe leaked away and the enemy grew fat.

sentences.zh: 忠規武節，未有如此其著者也。

translations.literal: In loyal counsel and martial integrity, none were so manifest as this.
translations.idiomatic: In steadfast loyalty and martial honor, none stood out as clearly as he.

sentences.zh: 武烈既沒，長沙桓王逸才命世，弱冠秀髮，招攬遺老，與之述業。

translations.literal: When Wu Lie had passed away, the Prince Huan of Changsha had transcendent talent and commanded the age; in his cap's weak years his hair was still fine; he summoned the surviving elders and with them carried forward the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian died, the Prince of Changsha, Sun Ce, appeared—a prodigy fitted for his time. Still in his twenties, he gathered the old loyalists of Wu and with them built anew what his father had begun.

sentences.zh: 神兵東驅，奮寡犯眾，攻無堅城之將，戰無交鋒之虜。

translations.literal: Divine hosts drove eastward; with few he struck many; in attack there were no generals of stubborn cities; in battle there were no foes who crossed blades.
translations.idiomatic: His army swept east: outnumbered, he struck numerically stronger foes. City walls yielded without stubborn defenders; battles ended before the enemy could close.

sentences.zh: 誅叛柔服，而江外底定；

translations.literal: He executed rebels and softened submission, and south of the Yangzi was brought to rest;
translations.idiomatic: He executed rebels and drew submitters gently to heel until the land beyond the Yangzi lay quiet;

sentences.zh: 飭法修師，則威德翕赫。

translations.literal: He ordered the laws and trained the troops, and awe and virtue blazed together.
translations.idiomatic: he tightened law and drilled the army, and majesty with virtue flared as one.

sentences.zh: 賓禮名賢，而張公為之雄；

translations.literal: He guest-treated famed worthies, and Lord Zhang was chief among them;
translations.idiomatic: He honored worthy men as guests, and Zhang Zhao towered above the rest;

sentences.zh: 交禦豪俊，而周瑜為之傑。

translations.literal: He associated with and employed heroic talents, and Zhou Yu was their outstanding man.
translations.idiomatic: he joined battle-side by side with bold spirits, and Zhou Yu stood first among them.

sentences.zh: 彼二君子皆弘敏而多奇，雅達而聰哲，故同方者以類附，等契者以氣集，江東蓋多士矣。

translations.literal: Those two gentlemen were both magnanimous and keen and full of wonders; elegant, penetrating, wise and discerning; therefore those of the same direction attached by kind, those of equal compact gathered by spirit—east of the Yangzi indeed had many gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were broad-minded, quick, and brilliant—refined, far-seeing, and wise. Men of like purpose flocked to them; kindred spirits rallied by sheer affinity. East of the Yangzi teemed with talent.

sentences.zh: 將北伐諸華，誅鉏幹紀，旋皇輿於夷庚，反帝坐於紫闥，挾天子以令諸侯，清天步而歸舊物。

translations.literal: He was about to march north to punish the Central States, execute those who violated the canon, turn the imperial carriage on the level road of Yi, return the emperor's seat to the purple chamber, clasp the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords, clear the heavenly steps and restore the former tokens.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to strike north into the heartland, root out traitors, wheel the imperial carriage onto the high road, set the throne again within the palace gates, take the emperor in hand and command the lords in his name, and sweep the realm clean until the Han regalia returned.

sentences.zh: 戎車既次，群凶側目，大業未就，中世而殞。

translations.literal: The war-chariots had already halted; the wicked looked sidelong; the great enterprise was not yet achieved; in mid-course he perished.
translations.idiomatic: His host was already on the march and rivals watched with fear, but the great work was unfinished—he died in his prime.

sentences.zh: 用集我大皇帝，以奇蹤襲逸軌，睿心因令圖，從政咨於故實，播憲稽乎遺風；

translations.literal: Thus was gathered our Great Emperor, who by marvelous traces followed the sweeping course, whose wise heart relied on excellent plans, who in governance consulted former precedents, who spread statutes and examined surviving customs;
translations.idiomatic: Then rose our Great Emperor Sun Quan, following that soaring example with designs of his own. His judgment rested on sound strategy; in government he weighed ancient precedent; in law he drew on customs handed down;

sentences.zh: 而加之以篤敬，申之以節儉，疇諮俊茂，好謀善斷，束帛旅於丘園，旌命交乎塗巷。

translations.literal: and added to this earnest reverence, extended frugality, consulted outstanding talents, loved planning and was good at deciding; bundled silk thronged in hills and gardens; summons flags crossed in lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: to these he joined deep reverence and thrift. He sought out every able mind, loved counsel, and decided swiftly. Gifts of silk piled up at recluses' doors; imperial summons crossed every lane.

sentences.zh: 故豪彥尋聲而響臻，志士晞光而景騖，異人輻輳，猛士如林。

translations.literal: Therefore heroic elites followed the sound and echoes gathered; aspirants gazed at the light and shadows raced; unusual men converged like spokes of a wheel; fierce warriors were like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes answered his call like echoes; men of purpose raced toward his light like horses chasing the sun. Strange talents crowded in; fierce soldiers stood thick as trees.

sentences.zh: 於是張公為師傅；

translations.literal: Then Lord Zhang became tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao became his tutor;

sentences.zh: 周瑜、陸公、魯肅、呂蒙之儔，入為腹心，出為股肱；

translations.literal: Zhou Yu, Lord Lu, Lu Su, Lu Meng and such entered as heart and belly, went out as thigh and arm;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu, Lu Su, Lu Meng, and Lord Lu Xun served him at court as his closest counselors and in the field as his strong right arms;

sentences.zh: 甘甯、淩統、程普、賀齊、硃桓、硃然之徒奮其威，韓當、潘璋、黃蓋、蔣欽、周泰之屬宣其力；

translations.literal: Gan Ning, Ling Tong, Cheng Pu, He Qi, Zhu Huan, Zhu Ran and such exerted their awe; Han Dang, Pan Zhang, Huang Gai, Jiang Qin, Zhou Tai and such displayed their strength;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning, Ling Tong, Cheng Pu, He Qi, Zhu Huan, Zhu Ran, and their like struck terror; Han Dang, Pan Zhang, Huang Gai, Jiang Qin, Zhou Tai, and their kind poured out sheer force;

sentences.zh: 風雅則諸葛瑾、張承、步騭以名聲光國，政事則顧雍、潘浚、呂范、呂岱以器任幹職，奇偉則虞翻、陸績、張惇以風義舉政，奉使則趙咨、沈珩以敏達延譽，術數則吳范、趙達以禨祥協德；

translations.literal: In refinement Zhuge Jin, Zhang Cheng, Bu Zhi by fame illuminated the state; in governance Gu Yong, Pan Jun, Lu Fan, Lu Dai by capacity held office and managed duties; in strangeness and greatness Yu Fan, Lu Ji, Zhang Dun by moral influence conducted policy; as envoys Zhao Zi, Shen Heng by keen penetration extended reputation; in arts of reckoning Wu Fan, Zhao Da by omens harmonized virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin, Zhang Cheng, and Bu Zhi lent the court literary grace; Gu Yong, Pan Jun, Lu Fan, and Lu Dai ran administration by sheer competence; Yu Fan, Lu Ji the younger, and Zhang Dun brought daring integrity to policy; Zhao Zi and Shen Heng won renown as nimble envoys; Wu Fan and Zhao Da read heaven's signs to match the ruler's virtue;

sentences.zh: 董襲、陳武殺身以衛主，駱統、劉基強諫以補過。

translations.literal: Dong Xi and Chen Wu killed themselves to guard the lord; Luo Tong and Liu Ji strongly remonstrated to mend faults.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi and Chen Wu gave their lives for their prince; Luo Tong and Liu Ji spoke bluntly to cure his missteps.

sentences.zh: 謀無遺計，舉不失策。

translations.literal: In planning none abandoned schemes; in action none missed measures.
translations.idiomatic: Plans left nothing unthought; every move matched the moment.

sentences.zh: 故遂割據山川，跨制荊、吳，而與天下爭衡矣。

translations.literal: Therefore they carved out hills and rivers, spanned and controlled Jing and Wu, and contended for balance with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they carved a realm between river and mountain, held Jing and Wu together, and faced the north as an equal power.

sentences.zh: 魏氏嘗藉戰勝之威，率百萬之師，浮鄧塞之舟，下漢陰之眾，羽楫萬計，龍躍順流，銳師千旅，武步原隰，謨臣盈室，武將連衡，喟然有吞江滸之志，壹宇宙之氣。

translations.literal: The Wei house once relied on the awe of victory in battle, led armies of a million, floated boats from Deng's barrier, brought down hosts from north of the Han; feathered oars numbered in the myriad; dragons leaped downcurrent; keen hosts by thousand brigades; martial tread on plain and marsh; planning ministers filled the chamber; martial generals linked in balance; sighingly they had the intent to swallow the river's bank and unify the pneuma of cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Wei once rode the prestige of victory: a million men, fleets launched from the Deng defiles, armies sweeping down from the Han northlands—oar blades beyond counting, hulls racing like dragons with the current, crack divisions marching plain and fen. Counselors packed their halls; generals stood ranged like stars. They meant to swallow the southern shore and knit the world under one breath.

sentences.zh: 而周瑜驅我偏師，黜之赤壁，喪旗亂轍，僅而獲免，收跡遠遁。

translations.literal: But Zhou Yu drove our detached army and defeated them at Red Cliffs; banners were lost and wheel-tracks confused; barely did they obtain escape; they gathered their traces and fled far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhou Yu led our southern army against them at Red Cliffs: their standards fell, their columns broke; they barely escaped with their lives and fled far north.

sentences.zh: 漢王亦憑帝王之號，帥巴、漢之人，乘危騁變，結壘千里，志報關羽之敗，圖收湘西之地。

translations.literal: The King of Han also relied on the title of emperor-king, led the people of Ba and Han, rode peril and exploited change, linked fortifications for a thousand li, aimed to avenge Guan Yu's defeat, planned to gather the lands west of the Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei likewise claimed imperial rank, marched the Ba and Han levies through crisis and sudden turns, and strung camps across a thousand li—intent on avenging Guan Yu's defeat and snatching the territory west of the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 而我陸公亦挫之西陵，覆師敗績，困而後濟，絕命永安。

translations.literal: And our Lord Lu also defeated them at Xiling; the army capsized and was routed; trapped, afterward they crossed—yet perished at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Our own Lu Xun broke them again at Xiling: whole armies drowned in rout; trapped and struggling to escape, Liu Bei ended his days at Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 續以濡須之寇，臨川摧銳；

translations.literal: Continuing with the invaders at Ruxu, along the river they shattered their keen edge;
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Ruxu, they lost their edge along the river;

sentences.zh: 蓬蘢之戰，孑輪不反。

translations.literal: in the battle of Penglong (variant place-name), not a single wheel returned.
translations.idiomatic: at Penglong not one chariot wheel rolled home.

sentences.zh: 由是二邦之將，喪氣挫鋒，勢<血醜>財匱，而吳莞然坐乘其弊，故魏人請好，漢氏乞盟，遂躋天號，鼎峙而立。

translations.literal: Thus the generals of the two states lost spirit and blunted edge; momentum flagged and funds were exhausted, yet Wu calmly sat and rode their exhaustion; therefore Wei men sought peace, the Han house begged alliance; thus they ascended to Heaven's title and stood tripod-like confronting.
translations.idiomatic: So both northern rivals lost heart and edge—their strength spent, their treasuries bare—while Wu watched at ease and turned their exhaustion to gain. Wei sued for peace; Shu begged for treaty. Thus Wu claimed the imperial title and stood as one leg of the tripod.

sentences.zh: 西界庸、益之郊，北裂淮、漢之涘，東苞百越之地，南括群蠻之表。

translations.literal: West it bordered the outskirts of Yong and Yi; north it split the banks of Huai and Han; east it embraced the lands of the Hundred Yue; south it enclosed the outer reaches of the mass of barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Its frontier touched Yong and Yi in the west, Huai and Han in the north, the Yue peoples in the east, and the southern tribes beyond.

sentences.zh: 於是講八代之禮，搜三王之樂，告類上帝，拱揖群後。

translations.literal: Then they lectured on the rites of eight dynasties, gathered the music of three kings, informed and categorized heaven above, bowed hands and yielded to the host of lords.
translations.idiomatic: They revived the rituals of ancient dynasties, gathered the music of the sage-kings, sacrificed to inform High Heaven, and received the feudal lords with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 武臣毅卒，循江而守；

translations.literal: Martial ministers and resolute soldiers followed the river and guarded;
translations.idiomatic: Fierce officers and hardened troops patrolled the long river;

sentences.zh: 長棘勁鎩，望猋而奮。

translations.literal: long halberds and keen spears, gazing at the gale-gust they roused themselves.
translations.idiomatic: halberds and spears leveled, each man springing to action at the first wind of war.

sentences.zh: 庶尹盡規于上，黎元展業於下，化協殊裔，風衍遐圻。

translations.literal: The multitude of directors all offered counsel above; the black-haired people expanded enterprise below; transformation harmonized distant descendants; wind extended to far borders.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers spoke freely at court; commoners flourished in the fields. Civilizing influence reached alien peoples; good order spread to the farthest marches.

sentences.zh: 乃俾一介行人，撫巡外域，巨象逸駿，擾於外閑，明珠瑋寶，耀於內府，珍瑰重跡而至，奇玩應響而赴；

translations.literal: Then they sent a single envoy to soothe and patrol outer regions; huge elephants and swift steeds crowded the outer enclosures; bright pearls and marvelous treasures dazzled the inner treasury; rare treasures arrived with overlapping tracks; curious playthings answered sound and hastened;
translations.idiomatic: A lone envoy could pacify distant lands; elephants and thoroughbreds crowded the imperial parks; pearls and jewels lit the palace stores; tribute gems arrived in endless trains; curiosities poured in at the slightest summons;

sentences.zh: 輶軒騁于南荒，沖輣息於朔野；

translations.literal: light carriages raced in the southern wastes; assault chariots rested on the northern plains;
translations.idiomatic: light carts swept the southern wilds; war wagons fell idle on the northern steppe;

sentences.zh: 黎庶免干戈之患，戎馬無晨服之虞，而帝業固矣。

translations.literal: the black-haired multitude were spared the calamity of shields and halberds; war-horses had no worry of morning harness; and the imperial enterprise was firm.
translations.idiomatic: the people knew little of arms; horses were seldom saddled at dawn—and the imperial house seemed secure.

sentences.zh: 大皇既沒，幼主蒞朝，奸回肆虐。

translations.literal: When the Great Emperor had passed away, the young lord assumed court; treacherous and crooked ones ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan died, a boy emperor sat the throne, and wicked men ran wild.

sentences.zh: 景皇聿興，虔修遺憲，政無大闕，守文之良主也。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing arose; reverently he cultivated the inherited statutes; government had no great defect—he was a good lord who guarded the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu then rose to the throne: he honored his predecessors' institutions and kept government largely sound—a worthy steward who preserved the founding pattern.

sentences.zh: 降及歸命之初，典刑未滅，故老猶存。

translations.literal: Down to the beginning of Surrendered Mandate, models were not yet extinguished; old servants still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the start of Sun Hao's reign, old institutions still lived and veterans yet remained.

sentences.zh: 大司馬陸公以文武熙朝，左丞相陸凱以謇諤盡規，而施績、範慎以威重顯，丁奉、鐘離斐以武毅稱，孟宗、丁固之徒為公卿，樓玄、賀邵之屬掌機事，元首雖病，股肱猶良。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Lord Lu by civil and martial matters illumined the court; Left Chancellor Lu Kai by blunt speech fulfilled counsel; while Shi Ji and Fan Shen were manifest by awe and weight; Ding Feng and Zhong Li Fei were famed by martial resolution; Meng Zong, Ding Gu and such became dukes and ministers; Lou Xuan, He Shao and such managed secret affairs; though the head ached, thigh and arm were still good.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang as grand marshal lent dignity to court and camp alike; Lu Kai as chief minister spoke blunt truth; Shi Ji and Fan Shen commanded respect; Ding Feng and Zhong Li Fei were famed as warriors; Meng Zong and Ding Gu rose to the highest offices; Lou Xuan and He Shao handled state secrets. The sovereign might be weak, but capable arms still served him.

sentences.zh: 爰逮末葉，群公既喪，然後黔首有瓦解之患，皇家有土崩之釁，曆命應化而微，王師躡運而發，卒散于陳，眾奔於邑，城池無籓籬之固，山川無溝阜之勢，非有工輸雲梯之械，智伯灌激之害，楚子築室之圍，燕人濟西之隊，軍未浹辰而社稷夷矣。

translations.literal: Coming down to the late leaf, when the host of dukes had already perished, then the black-haired people had the calamity of tile-dissolution; the imperial house had the crack of earth-collapse; the rotating mandate responded to transformation and became faint; royal armies trod fortune and set forth; soldiers scattered at Chen, crowds fled in districts; city walls had no hedge-fence solidity; hills and streams had no ditch-mound advantage—there were no Gongshu cloud-ladder machines, no Zhi Bo irrigation harms, no Chu prince wall-building sieges, no Yan men west-of-Ji formations—before twelve days the army had ended and altars of soil and grain were levelled.
translations.idiomatic: But by the final years those pillars were gone. The people scattered like tiles; the throne crumbled like earth. Heaven's favor faded; Jin's hosts marched with destiny. Troops melted away in the field; refugees clogged the towns. Walls offered no hedge of defense; rivers no trench or hill to rely on—and yet no enemy needed Gongshu's siege ladders, Zhi Bo's drowned cities, Chu-style slow sieges, or Yan-style western diversions. Within twelve days the altars lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 雖忠臣孤憤，烈士死節，將奚救哉！

translations.literal: Although loyal ministers nursed solitary rage, ardent knights died for integrity—how could they save it!
translations.idiomatic: What could loyal ministers do but rage alone, what could heroes do but die for honor—when nothing could save the state?

sentences.zh: 夫曹、劉之將非一世所選，向時之師無曩日之眾，戰守之道抑有前符，險阻之利俄然未改，而成敗貿理，古今詭趣，何哉？

translations.literal: Now the generals of Cao and Liu were not chosen in one generation; the armies of recent times did not have the multitudes of former days; the ways of battle and defense likewise had former correspondences; the advantages of peril and obstruction suddenly were not changed—yet victory and defeat exchanged principle; ancient and modern move strangely—why?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei and Liu Shu's commanders were not raised in a single generation; later armies were smaller than those old hosts. The arts of attack and defense had not changed; terrain favored the south as before—yet fortune reversed. Why do success and failure trade places so strangely between past and present?

sentences.zh: 彼此之化殊，授任之才異也。

translations.literal: The transformation of each other was different; the talents entrusted differed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the temper of the times differed, and the men placed in charge were not the same.

sentences.zh: 其下篇曰：

translations.literal: The lower piece says:
translations.idiomatic: The second essay reads:

sentences.zh: 昔三方之王也，魏人據中夏，漢氏有岷、益，吳制荊、揚而掩有交、廣。

translations.literal: Formerly when the three sides were kings: Wei men occupied the Central Plains; the Han house held Min and Yi; Wu controlled Jing and Yang and covered Jiao and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm split three ways, Wei held the heartland, Shu the Min and Yi basins, and Wu Jing and Yang with Jiao and Guang besides.

sentences.zh: 曹氏雖功濟諸華，虐亦深矣，其人怨。

translations.literal: Although the Cao house by merit aided the Hua states, their cruelty was also deep; the people resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei may have brought order to the north, but their cruelty ran deep and the people nursed grudges.

sentences.zh: 劉翁因險以飾智，功已薄矣，其俗陋。

translations.literal: The old Liu relied on peril to adorn cleverness; merit was already thin; their customs were coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Old Liu Bei traded on mountain barriers to seem clever; his achievement was slight and his realm coarse in habit.

sentences.zh: 夫吳，桓王基之以武，太祖成之以德，聰明睿達，懿度弘遠矣。

translations.literal: As for Wu, the Prince Huan founded it with arms, the Grand Ancestor completed it with virtue—bright, wise, penetrating and far-reaching; excellent measure vast and distant.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was another matter: Sun Ce laid its foundations in war, Sun Quan perfected it in virtue—clear-sighted, magnanimous, with breadth of vision few could match.

sentences.zh: 其求賢如弗及，血阝人如稚子，接士盡盛德之容，親仁罄丹府之愛。

translations.literal: His seeking worthies was as if he could not catch up; cherishing people as young children; receiving gentlemen he exhausted the bearing of abundant virtue; drawing near the humane he emptied his red chamber's love.
translations.idiomatic: He sought worthy men as if always behindhand; he cherished the people like children. With scholars he showed unstinting courtesy; with the humane he shared every secret warmth.

sentences.zh: 拔呂蒙於戎行，試潘浚於系虜。

translations.literal: He raised Lü Meng from the warrior ranks; tried Pan Jun among bound captives.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled Lü Meng from the ranks and tried Pan Jun even while the man was prisoner.

sentences.zh: 推誠信士，不恤人之我欺；

translations.literal: He pushed sincerity and trusted gentlemen; he did not fret that others might deceive him;
translations.idiomatic: He trusted men with open sincerity and never troubled himself over whether they might deceive him;

sentences.zh: 量能授器，不患權之我偪。

translations.literal: He measured capacity and bestowed tools; he did not worry that power pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: he fitted office to talent and never feared that ministers might crowd him out.

sentences.zh: 執鞭鞠躬，以重陸公之威；

translations.literal: He held whip and bowed the body, thereby to weight Lord Lu's awe;
translations.idiomatic: He took the driver's whip and bowed low to magnify Lu Xun's authority;

sentences.zh: 悉委武衛，以濟周瑜之師。

translations.literal: He wholly entrusted martial guards, thereby to aid Zhou Yu's army.
translations.idiomatic: he stripped the palace guard to reinforce Zhou Yu's campaign.

sentences.zh: 卑宮菲食，豐功臣之賞；

translations.literal: Low palace and meager food—rich were the rewards of merit ministers;
translations.idiomatic: He kept his halls modest and his table plain while lavishing rewards on those who earned them;

sentences.zh: 披懷虛己，納謨士之算。

translations.literal: He opened his breast and emptied himself; he admitted planning gentlemen's calculations.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his heart and humbled himself before good counsel.

sentences.zh: 故魯肅一面而自托，士燮蒙險而效命。

translations.literal: Therefore Lu Su on one meeting entrusted himself; Shi Xie braved peril and rendered mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su pledged himself after a single audience; Shi Xie crossed deadly ground to answer his call.

sentences.zh: 高張公之德，而省游田之娛；

translations.literal: He elevated Lord Zhang's virtue and reduced roaming-hunt pleasures;
translations.idiomatic: He honored Zhang Zhao's integrity and cut back the pleasures of the hunt;

sentences.zh: 賢諸葛之言，而割情欲之歡；

translations.literal: He deemed Zhuge's words worthy and cut passionate-desire joys;
translations.idiomatic: he prized Zhuge Jin's advice and put aside private indulgence;

sentences.zh: 感陸公之規，而除刑法之煩；

translations.literal: He was moved by Lord Lu's regulations and removed penal law's annoyances;
translations.idiomatic: moved by Lu Xun's memorials, he swept away needless severity in punishment;

sentences.zh: 奇劉基之議，而作三爵之誓；

translations.literal: He wondered at Liu Ji's proposal and made the oath of three cups;
translations.idiomatic: he marveled at Liu Ji's counsel and swore the oath of the three goblets;

sentences.zh: 屏氣跼蹐，以伺子明之疾；

translations.literal: He held breath and walked bent to wait on Ziming's illness;
translations.idiomatic: he held his breath and tiptoed to nurse Lü Meng in his illness;

sentences.zh: 分滋損甘，以育淩統之孤；

translations.literal: He divided sweet and reduced sweet to nurture Ling Tong's orphans;
translations.idiomatic: he gave his own sweet portions to raise Ling Tong's orphaned children;

sentences.zh: 登壇慷愾，歸魯子之功；

translations.literal: Ascending the altar, generous indignation—he returned merit to Master Lu;
translations.idiomatic: on the altar he spoke with fierce gratitude and gave Lu Su full credit for his deeds;

sentences.zh: 削投怨言，信子瑜之節。

translations.literal: He carved away thrown resentful words; he trusted Ziyu's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: he struck harsh words from edicts and trusted Zhuge Jin's steadfast honor.

sentences.zh: 是以忠臣競盡其謨，志士咸得肆力，洪規遠略，固不厭夫區區者也。

translations.literal: Therefore loyal ministers vied to exhaust their counsels; aspirant knights all obtained scope for strength; great norms and far plans—solidly they did not stint on trifles.
translations.idiomatic: So loyal officers strained every faculty for him; men of purpose found room to give their all. Great design and long vision—nothing petty escaped his care.

sentences.zh: 故百官苟合，庶務未遑。

translations.literal: Therefore the hundred offices barely combined; myriad tasks had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Officialdom barely kept pace; routine business never quite caught up.

sentences.zh: 初都建鄴，群臣請備禮秩，天子辭而弗許，曰：「天下其謂朕何！

translations.literal: When first they capitalled at Jianye, the host of ministers requested complete ritual ranks; the Son of Heaven declined and did not permit, saying: 'What will the realm say of Us!
translations.idiomatic: When they first made Jianye the capital, ministers begged for full court ceremonial. The sovereign refused: 'What would the empire say of me

sentences.zh: 」宮室輿服，蓋慊如也。

translations.literal: ' Palaces and chambers, carriages and robes—generally were sparing thus.
translations.idiomatic: if I indulged?' Palaces, equipage, and dress stayed deliberately plain.

sentences.zh: 爰及中葉，天人之分既定，故百度之缺粗修，雖醲化懿綱，未齒乎上代，抑其體國經邦之具，亦足以為政矣。

translations.literal: Down to the middle leaf, heaven and man's divisions already fixed, therefore the hundred measures' gaps were roughly repaired; although rich transformation and fine norms did not rank with upper ages, yet their tools for embodying state and regulating state were also sufficient to govern.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-reign heaven's mandate and human affairs had settled; policy gaps were roughly mended. Their refinement never matched antiquity's golden age, yet the instruments of statecraft sufficed to rule.

sentences.zh: 地方幾萬里，帶甲將百萬，其野沃，其兵練，其器利，其財豐；

translations.literal: The territory was nearly ten thousand li; armored soldiers approached a million; its wilds were fertile; its troops drilled; its weapons sharp; its wealth abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Their territory spanned tens of thousands of li; nearly a million men bore arms. The soil was rich, soldiers veteran, weapons keen, treasuries full;

sentences.zh: 東負滄海，西阻險塞，長江制其區宇，峻山帶其封域，國家之利未見有弘於茲者也。

translations.literal: East it backed on the grey sea; west it blocked with perilous passes; the long river regulated its regions; steep mountains girded its sealed territory—of advantages for the state, none have been seen ampler than this.
translations.idiomatic: east lay the sea, west rugged passes; the Yangzi hemmed their domain and mountains walled their borders—no kingdom ever held stronger natural gifts.

sentences.zh: 借使守之以道，禦之以術，敦率遺典，勤人謹政，修定策，守常險，則可以長世永年，未有危亡之患也。

translations.literal: Suppose they had guarded it with the Way, defended it with method, urged and led inherited canons, diligently governed people and careful policy, cultivated settled plans, guarded constant perils—then they could have long generations and enduring years; there would have been no danger of peril and death.
translations.idiomatic: Had they held this with sound principle, governed with art, honored inherited statute, kept administration careful and people diligent, refined stable strategy, and trusted their terrain— they might have lasted age upon age without fear of ruin.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「吳、蜀脣齒之國也，夫蜀滅吳亡，理則然矣。

translations.literal: Someone said: 'Wu and Shu are lip-and-teeth states; when Shu perished Wu died—by principle it is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: 'Wu and Shu were lip and teeth—once Shu fell, Wu was doomed. That sounds reasonable.

sentences.zh: 」夫蜀，蓋籓援之與國，而非吳人之存亡也。

translations.literal: ' Shu was but a screen-support ally-state; it was not Wu men's survival or death.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was only a shield and ally—hardly the pivot of Wu's fate.

sentences.zh: 其郊境之接，重山積險，陸無長轂之徑；

translations.literal: Where their border march connected, layered mountains piled peril; on land there were no long axle-paths;
translations.idiomatic: Between them rose range upon range—no corridor for heavy chariots;

sentences.zh: 川厄流迅，水有驚波之艱。

translations.literal: rivers were blocked and currents swift; on water there was the hardship of startling waves.
translations.idiomatic: rivers ran swift through narrows where waves could smash any fleet.

sentences.zh: 雖有銳師百萬，啟行不過千夫；

translations.literal: Although there were keen hosts of a million, setting forth did not exceed a thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Even a million veterans could feed only a thousand men forward along those roads;

sentences.zh: 軸轤千里，前驅不過百艦。

translations.literal: Though fleets might reach a thousand li of linked hulls, the leading ships numbered barely a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: oared fleets might string out endlessly downriver, yet no more than a hundred hulls could fight abreast at the van.

sentences.zh: 故劉氏之伐，陸公喻之長蛇，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu's expedition—Lord Lu compared it to a long snake—such was the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun likened Liu Bei's invasion to a long snake—terrain alone dictated it.

sentences.zh: 昔蜀之初亡，朝臣異謀，或欲積石以險其流，或欲機械以禦其變。

translations.literal: Formerly when Shu first perished, court ministers had differing plans—some wished to pile stones to peril its current; some wished machines to ward its changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first fell, Wu's court argued—some urged damming the Yangzi with stone, others clever machines to meet whatever came.

sentences.zh: 天子總群議以諮之大司馬陸公，公以四瀆天地之所以節宣其氣，固無可遏之理，而機械則彼我所共，彼若棄長技以就所屈，即荊、楚而爭舟楫之用，是天贊我也，將謹守峽口以待擒耳。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven gathered the host of deliberations and consulted Grand Marshal Lord Lu. The lord said: the four waterways are what heaven and earth use to regulate and vent their qi—there is fundamentally no principle by which they can be dammed. As for machines, those are shared by them and us; if they abandon long skills to submit to constrained ground, then coming to Jing and Chu they contest boat and oar use—this is heaven aiding us; we need only strictly guard the gorge mouth to await capture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put the debate to Lu Kang. Lu answered: the great rivers vent heaven and earth—no dam can long hold them back. Engines of war both sides know; if Jin abandons its strengths to fight where river craft decide the battle on former Chu ground, heaven favors Wu—we need only seal the gorges and wait.

sentences.zh: 逮步闡之亂，憑寶城以延強寇，資重幣以誘群蠻。

translations.literal: Coming to Bu Chan's rebellion, relying on precious cities to draw out strong invaders, supplying heavy currency to entice the mass of barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bu Chan rebelled, trusting fortress walls to stall a mighty foe and rich bribes to win the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 于時大邦之眾，雲翔電發，懸旍江介，築壘遵渚，衿帶要害，以止吳人之西，巴、漢舟師，沿江東下。

translations.literal: At that time the great state's multitudes, cloud-soaring and lightning-rising, hung banners at the river's midst, built fortifications along islets, girdled vital points, to stop Wu men's west; Ba and Han boat armies along the river went east down.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jin's host rose like storm clouds: flags lined the midstream, forts studded the shoals, every choke point held to bar Wu from the west while Ba and Han fleets bore down the river.

sentences.zh: 陸公偏師三萬，北據東坑，深溝高壘，按甲養威。

translations.literal: Lord Lu's detached army thirty thousand, north occupying Dongkeng, deep ditches and high ramparts, pressing armor and nurturing awe.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang led thirty thousand to hold Dongkeng in the north—deep moats, high walls, blades sheathed while prestige ripened.

sentences.zh: 反虜宛跡待戮，而不敢北窺生路，強寇敗績宵遁，喪師太半。

translations.literal: The rebellious captives lingered traces awaiting execution, yet did not dare northward peep for paths of life; the strong invaders routed fled by night, losing armies more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels huddled in their holes awaiting slaughter and dared not strike north for escape; the mighty foe broke at night and fled, leaving more than half his army dead.

sentences.zh: 分命銳師五千，西禦水軍，東西同捷，獻俘萬計。

translations.literal: Separately he ordered five thousand crack troops west to resist the water army; east and west alike scored victories; captives presented numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He detached five thousand picked troops to hold the western fleet; east and west both reported victories, and prisoners handed up ran to the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 信哉賢人之謀，豈欺我哉！

translations.literal: True indeed is the counsel of worthies—would they deceive us!
translations.idiomatic: So true was worthies' counsel—surely they did not mislead us!

sentences.zh: 自是烽燧罕驚，封域寡虞。

translations.literal: From this beacon fires rarely alarmed; sealed borders seldom had anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: After that alarm fires seldom blazed along the frontier; the realm rarely faced alarm.

sentences.zh: 陸公沒而潛謀兆，吳釁深而六師駭。

translations.literal: When Lord Lu died hidden plots began to show; Wu's breach grew deep and the six armies trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang's death opened the door to intrigue; Wu's fatal weakness deepened and every army felt the shock.

sentences.zh: 夫太康之役，眾未盛乎曩日之師；

translations.literal: As for the Taikang campaign, the hosts were not greater than the armies of earlier days;
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Taikang invasion: Jin's host was no larger than armies Wu had faced before;

sentences.zh: 廣州之亂，禍有愈乎向時之難，而邦家顛覆，宗廟為墟。

translations.literal: the Guangzhou rebellion—was calamity worse than former crises?—yet state and house were overturned, ancestral temples became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: the Guangzhou rising hurt worse than earlier shocks—yet in the end the dynasty fell and its temples lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 「人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁」，不其然歟！

translations.literal: "When those men pass away, the state wastes with grief"—is it not thus!
translations.idiomatic: "When such men are gone, the land itself sickens"—was it not exactly so!

sentences.zh: 《易》曰「湯、武革命順乎天」，或曰「亂不極則治不形」，言帝王之因天時也。

translations.literal: The Changes says "Tang and Wu's revolution accorded with Heaven"; someone says "without disorder reaching its extreme, order does not appear"—this speaks of emperors and kings conforming to Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says Tang and Wu's revolution followed Heaven's mandate; others say order does not emerge until chaos reaches its limit—meaning kings must ride the season Heaven grants.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰「天時不如地利」，《易》曰「王侯設險以守其國」，言為國之恃險也。

translations.literal: The ancients said "seasonal Heaven is not as good as advantageous terrain"; the Changes says "kings and marquises set perilous defenses to guard their states"—this speaks of relying on terrain in governing a state.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients held that Heaven's timing yields to terrain; the Changes adds that lords raise barriers to shield their realms—terrain is the state's buckler.

sentences.zh: 又曰「地利不如人和」，「在德不在險」，言守險之在人也。

translations.literal: It also says "advantageous terrain is not as good as human harmony"; "it lies in virtue, not in peril"—this speaks of guarding peril lying in men.
translations.idiomatic: It also says terrain bows to human harmony and that security rests in virtue, not cliffs—meaning defenses live or die with the men who hold them.

sentences.zh: 吳之興也，參而由焉，孫卿所謂合其參者也。

translations.literal: In Wu's rise, it participated by these three—what Sun Qing called combining the three.
translations.idiomatic: Wu rose because all three factors worked together—what Xunzi meant by uniting Heaven, earth, and men.

sentences.zh: 及其亡也，恃險而已，又孫卿所謂舍其參者也。

translations.literal: At its fall it relied on peril alone—again what Sun Qing called abandoning the three.
translations.idiomatic: When it fell, Wu trusted nothing but rivers and mountains—exactly Xunzi's warning about throwing the three away.

sentences.zh: 夫四州之萌非無眾也，大江以南非乏俊也，山川之險易守也，勁利之器易用也，先政之策易修也，功不興而禍遘何哉？

translations.literal: The sprouts of four provinces were not without multitude; south of the Great River talents were not lacking; mountains and rivers' peril was easy to defend; keen sharp weapons easy to use; former policies easy to restore—why did merit not rise yet calamity meet?
translations.idiomatic: The south still had multitudes and talent; rivers and hills were easy to hold, arms ready to hand, old policies easy to revive—why then did fortune fail and ruin strike?

sentences.zh: 所以用之者失也。

translations.literal: Those who employed them failed.
translations.idiomatic: Because those who wielded these advantages misused them.

sentences.zh: 故先王達經國之長規，審存亡之至數，謙己以安百姓，敦惠以致人和，寬沖以誘俊乂之謀，慈和以結士庶之愛。

translations.literal: Therefore former kings comprehended the long norms for ordering the state, examined the utmost reckonings of survival and perdition, humbled themselves to pacify the hundred surnames, enriched kindness to bring human harmony, broadened modesty to entice plans from outstanding talents, used compassion and harmony to bind love of gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings grasped enduring principles of government and the calculus of survival. They humbled themselves to steady the people, piled kindness high to win harmony, stayed open and yielding to draw counsel from worthies, and ruled with gentleness so gentle and commoner alike loved them.

sentences.zh: 是以其安也，則黎元與之同慶，及其危也，則兆庶與之同患。

translations.literal: Therefore in their peace the black-haired shared celebration; in their peril the myriad masses shared grief.
translations.idiomatic: In peace the people rejoiced with the throne; in danger they suffered with it.

sentences.zh: 安與眾同慶，則其危不可得也；

translations.literal: If in peace they share celebration with the multitude, peril cannot obtain them;
translations.idiomatic: Share joy with the people in good times, and disaster cannot take you unawares;

sentences.zh: 危與下同患，則其難不足血阝也。

translations.literal: If in peril they share grief with those below, the hardship is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Share peril with those below in dark hours, and hardship loses its sting.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故能保其社稷而固其土宇，《麥秀》無悲殷之思，《黍離》無湣周之感也。

translations.literal: Being thus, therefore they could preserve their altars of soil and grain and firm their territory—no pity-Shang thoughts in "Wheat Effer"; no pity-Zhou feelings in "Millet Stalk."
translations.idiomatic: That is how altars and territory endure—never needing the lament of "The Wheat in Ear" for Yin nor the sorrow of "Millet Stalk" for Zhou.

sentences.zh: 至太康末，與弟雲俱入洛，造太常張華。

translations.literal: By late Taikang end, together with his younger brother Yun he entered Luoyang and visited Minister Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the end of the Taikang era he traveled to Luoyang with his brother Lu Yun and called on the Chamberlain Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 華素重其名，如舊相識，曰：「伐吳之役，利獲二俊。

translations.literal: Hua always esteemed his name; like old acquaintances he said: "In the Wu expedition's profit we gained two outstanding men."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua had long admired his reputation and greeted him like an old friend. "The campaign against Wu," he said, "paid us twice over with brilliant recruits."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗詣侍中王濟，濟指羊酪謂機曰：「卿吳中何以敵此？

translations.literal: He also once visited attendant Wang Ji; Ji pointed at sheep cheese and said to Ji: "How does your Wu match this?"
translations.idiomatic: Another time he visited the imperial attendant Wang Ji, who pointed at a dish of sheep-milk cheese and asked, "What in Wu can rival this?"

sentences.zh: 」答云：「千里蓴羹，未下鹽豉。

translations.literal: He answered saying: "Thousand-li water-shield soup—not yet salt and fermented beans cast in."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji replied, "A bowl of water-shield broth from a thousand li away—salt and fermented beans have yet to touch it."

sentences.zh: 」時人稱為名對。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised it as a famous reply.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries hailed it as a perfect riposte.

sentences.zh: 張華薦之諸公。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua recommended him to the high dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua recommended him to the ranking ministers.

sentences.zh: 後太傅楊駿辟為祭酒。

translations.literal: Later Grand Tutor Yang Jun summoned him as libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Later Grand Tutor Yang Jun appointed him libationer of his bureau.

sentences.zh: 會駿誅，累遷太子洗馬、著作郎。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, he successively rose to Crown Prince attendant groom and editorial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell to execution, Lu Ji rose step by step to groom of the heir apparent and secretary in the editorial office.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧志於眾中問機曰：「陸遜、陸抗於君近遠？

translations.literal: Fan Yang Lu Zhi asked Ji in the crowd: "Lu Xun and Lu Kang—to you are they close or distant?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of Fanyang asked him before company, "How were Lu Xun and Lu Kang related to you?"

sentences.zh: 」機曰：「如君于盧毓、盧廷。

translations.literal: Ji said: "As you are to Lu Yu and Lu Ting."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji answered, "As you stand to Lu Yu and Lu Ting."

sentences.zh: 」志默然。

translations.literal: Zhi fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said nothing.

sentences.zh: 既起，雲謂機曰：「殊邦遐遠，容不相悉，何至於此！

translations.literal: After rising, Yun said to Ji: "Different lands, far apart—we might not know each other—but why go this far!"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Lu Yun said to him, "We come from distant lands; perhaps he truly did not know—yet why answer so sharply?"

sentences.zh: 」機曰：「我父祖名播四海，寧不知邪！

translations.literal: Ji said: "My father and grandfather's names spread within the four seas—would he truly not know!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji replied, "My father's and grandfather's fame fills the realm—could he really be ignorant?"

sentences.zh: 」議者以此定二陸之優劣。

translations.literal: Discussers by this settled the relative superiority of the two Lu brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers took this exchange as the measure of the two brothers' temperaments.

sentences.zh: 吳王晏出鎮淮南，以機為郎中令，遷尚書中兵郎，轉殿中郎。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Yan went out to garrison Huainan and appointed Ji as palace superintendent; he rose to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Secretariat and transferred to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yan of Wu went out to command Huainan, he named Lu Ji superintendent of his household; Lu Ji then rose through secretary posts on the military desk and moved into the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫輔政，引為相國參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun aided governance and drew him in as counselor of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun of Zhao became regent, he brought Lu Ji onto staff as counselor of the counselor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 豫誅賈謐功，賜爵關中侯。

translations.literal: For participating in executing Jia Mi's merit, he was granted noble rank Marquis Within-the-Passes.
translations.idiomatic: For helping eliminate Jia Mi he received the noble title Marquis of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 倫將篡位，以為中書郎。

translations.literal: When Lun was about to usurp the throne, he appointed him gentleman of the palace writers.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun prepared to seize the throne he appointed Lu Ji gentleman at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 倫之誅也，齊王冏以機職在中書，九錫文及禪詔疑機與焉，遂收機等九人付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, Prince Qi Jiong because Ji's office was in the Secretariat and suspected Ji participated in the nine-bestowals document and abdication edict, therefore seized Ji and nine others and handed them to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun fell, Prince Jiong of Qi suspected Lu Ji—still serving at the Secretariat—of drafting the nine-insignia memorial and abdication edict, so he arrested Lu Ji and eight others and sent them to the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 賴成都王穎、吳王晏並救理之，得減死徙邊，遇赦而止。

translations.literal: Thanks to Prince Chengdu Ying and Prince Wu Yan together rescuing and reasoning for them, they obtained commuted death and exile to the frontier; encountering amnesty they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chengdu and Prince Yan of Wu intervened to spare their lives; their sentence was reduced to exile on the frontier, though an amnesty soon halted even that.

sentences.zh: 初機有駿犬，名曰黃耳，甚愛之。

translations.literal: Formerly Ji had a swift dog named Yellow Ear; he greatly loved it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji once owned a fleet hound named Yellow Ear that he adored.

sentences.zh: 既而羈寓京師，久無家問，笑語犬曰：「我家絕無書信，汝能齎書取消息不？

translations.literal: Afterward sojourning bound in the capital, long without news from home, he laughed and told the dog: "My house absolutely lacks letters—can you carry letters and fetch news?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, stalled in the capital without word from home, he teased the dog: "No letters reach me—could you carry one home and bring back a reply?"

sentences.zh: 」犬搖尾作聲。

translations.literal: The dog wagged its tail and made sound.
translations.idiomatic: The dog barked and thumped its tail.

sentences.zh: 機乃為書以竹筒盛之而系其頸，犬尋路南走，遂至其家，得報還洛。

translations.literal: Ji then wrote a letter, put it in a bamboo tube and tied it on its neck; the dog sought the road south and arrived at his house, obtained reply and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji rolled a letter into a bamboo tube, lashed it around the dog's neck, and sent him south. The hound found his way home, collected a reply, and trotted back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其後因以為常。

translations.literal: Afterward by this they made it customary.
translations.idiomatic: After that they relied on the dog whenever mail was needed.

sentences.zh: 時中國多難，顧榮、戴若思等咸勸機還吳，機負其才望，而志匡世難，故不從。

translations.literal: At that time the central lands had many calamities; Gu Rong, Dai Ruosi and such all urged Ji to return to Wu; Ji bore his talent and reputation and aimed to rectify the age's calamities, therefore did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The north was riven by crisis; Gu Rong, Dai Yong, and others urged Lu Ji to retreat south, but pride in his gifts and a desire to mend the age kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 冏既矜功自伐，受爵不讓，機惡之，作《豪士賦》以刺焉。

translations.literal: Jiong having boasted of merit and praised himself, accepting noble rank without yielding, Ji hated him and composed Rhapsody on the Proud Knight to satirize him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiong swaggered over his deeds and seized honors without modesty. Lu Ji despised him and wrote his Rhapsody on the Magnate to needle him.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface says:
translations.idiomatic: The preface runs:

sentences.zh: 夫立德之基有常，而建功之路不一。

translations.literal: The foundation of establishing virtue has constancy, yet the roads of establishing merit are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue rests on fixed roots, yet merit may be won by many paths.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 修心以為量者存乎我，因物以成務者系乎彼。

translations.literal: Cultivating the heart to make measure lies in us; relying on things to complete tasks ties to those others.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivating the heart lies entirely within us; accomplishing deeds through circumstance depends on what lies beyond.

sentences.zh: 存乎我者，隆殺止乎其域；

translations.literal: What lies in us—rise and kill stop within its boundary;
translations.idiomatic: What rests with us alone rises or falls within narrow bounds;

sentences.zh: 系乎彼者，豐約惟所遭遇。

translations.literal: what ties to those others—fullness and contraction follow only what is encountered.
translations.idiomatic: what rides on the world waxes or wanes with sheer accident.

sentences.zh: 落葉俟微飆以隕，而風之力蓋寡；

translations.literal: Fallen leaves await slight whirlwind to fall, yet wind's power is generally slight;
translations.idiomatic: Leaves fall when a breeze stirs—yet the gust itself is slight;

sentences.zh: 孟嘗遭雍門以泣，而琴之感以末。

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang encountered Yongmen thereby to weep, yet the qin's moving power ended slight.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang wept when Yongmen Zhou played—but the last notes barely brushed his heart.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 欲隕之葉無所假烈風，將墜之泣不足煩哀響也。

translations.literal: Leaves about to fall need borrow no fierce wind; tears about to fall need not trouble mournful echoes.
translations.idiomatic: A leaf ready to drop needs no gale; tears already falling need no funeral song.

sentences.zh: 是故苟時啟於天，理盡於人，庸夫可以濟聖賢之功，鬥筲可以定烈士之業。

translations.literal: Therefore if the season opens from Heaven and principle is exhausted in men, then mediocre husbands can aid sage-worthies' merit; dipper-measure vessels can settle ardent knights' enterprises.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven opens the moment and human effort matches it, even common men may finish the labors of sages; even petty vessels may seal a hero's deed.

sentences.zh: 故曰「才不半古，功已倍之」，蓋得之于時世也。

translations.literal: Thus it is said "talent not half of antiquity's, yet merit already doubles theirs"—generally obtained from the age's timeliness.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that men with half the talent of the ancients double their deeds—they owe it to the hour history gives them.

sentences.zh: 曆觀今古，徼一時之功而居伊、周之位者有矣。

translations.literal: Surveying past and present, those who by luck at one time's merit occupy Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou's positions—there have been such.
translations.idiomatic: History shows men who seized fleeting luck and climbed to seats worthy of Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 夫我之自我，智士猶嬰其累；

translations.literal: As for self's selfhood, wise men still bear its burden;
translations.idiomatic: Even wise men are trapped by their sense of self;

sentences.zh: 物之相物，昆蟲皆有此情。

translations.literal: Things' mutual thing-ing—even insects all have this sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: creatures judging one another feel the same—insects included.

sentences.zh: 夫以自我之量而挾非常之勳，神器暉其顧眄，萬物隨其俯仰，心玩居常之安，耳飽從諛之說，豈識乎功在身外，任出才表者哉！

translations.literal: Now using self's measure while clasping extraordinary merit—the divine vessel gleams in his glance; myriad things follow his nod and shake; his heart toys with dwelling-in-constant peace; his ears are sated with following-flattery speech—how could he recognize merit lying outside the body, appointment exceeding talent's surface!
translations.idiomatic: Attach outsized deeds to an inflated self, let regalia glitter with every glance, let the world sway as you nod—stay drunk on ease and flattery, and you will never see merit as something beyond yourself or office as larger than your gifts.

sentences.zh: 且好榮惡辱，有生之所大期，忌盈害上，鬼神猶且不免，人主操其常柄，天下服其大節，故曰天可仇乎。

translations.literal: Moreover loving glory and hating shame is the great expectation of the living; envying fullness and harming superiors—even ghosts and spirits still do not avoid it; the lord of men wields his constant handle; the realm submits to his great nodes—thus it is said: can Heaven be resented?
translations.idiomatic: All living souls crave honor and dread shame; even spirits punish pride that wounds superiors. The emperor holds the supreme grip; the realm bows to his authority—can anyone blame Heaven when disaster follows?

sentences.zh: 而時有玄服荷戟，立乎廟門之下，援旗誓眾，奮於阡陌之上，況乎世主制命，自下裁物者乎！

translations.literal: Yet there are times when black-robed halberd-bearers stand below the temple gate, grasp banner and swear the host, rouse on paths between fields—how much more when the age's lord controls mandate and from below judges things!
translations.idiomatic: Common soldiers in temple guard still seize standards and rally the ranks—how much more dangerous when the age itself lets lesser men steer the realm.

sentences.zh: 廣樹恩不足以敵怨，勤興利不足以補害，故曰代大匠斫者必傷其手。

translations.literal: Broad planting kindness is insufficient to resist resentment; diligent raising profit is insufficient to mend harm—thus it is said he who for the great carpenter chops must wound his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Kindness heaped high cannot drown out hate; profit poured out cannot heal every wound—hence the warning that whoever swings the master carpenter's axe cuts his own hand.

sentences.zh: 且夫政由甯氏，忠臣所以慷慨；

translations.literal: Moreover when government proceeds through the Ning clan, loyal ministers therefore grow indignant;
translations.idiomatic: When ministers of Wei ran the state through the Ning family, loyal hearts boiled—

sentences.zh: 祭則寡人，人主所不久堪。

translations.literal: "At sacrifice it is the solitary man"—what the lord of men cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: yet at sacrifice only the ruler stood titled "the solitary"—no sovereign long tolerates such hollowing.

sentences.zh: 是以君奭怏怏，不悅公旦之舉；

translations.literal: Therefore Lord Shi was displeased, did not approve Duke Dan's measures;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi sulked because he distrusted the Duke of Zhou's schemes;

sentences.zh: 高平師師，側目博陸之勢。

translations.literal: Gaoping's hosts glared sidelong at Bolu's power.
translations.idiomatic: at Gaoping every soldier glared sideways at Huo Guang's grip on power.

sentences.zh: 而成王不遣嫌吝于懷，宣帝若負芒刺於背，非其然者歟？

translations.literal: Yet King Cheng did not send suspicion-grudging from his breast; Emperor Xuan seemed to bear awl-thorns on his back—is it not thus?
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng nursed no lasting grudge; Emperor Xuan felt barbs between his shoulders—could trust survive anything less?

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 光于四表，德莫富焉。

translations.literal: Radiance to the four outer zones—virtue none richer.
translations.idiomatic: His brightness reached the four seas—no virtue richer.

sentences.zh: 王曰叔父，親莫昵焉。

translations.literal: "King" says "uncle"—kinship none closer.
translations.idiomatic: The king called him uncle—no bond closer.

sentences.zh: 登帝天位，功莫厚焉。

translations.literal: Ascending emperor heaven's seat—merit none thicker.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the throne—no merit weightier.

sentences.zh: 守節沒齒，忠莫至焉。

translations.literal: Guarding integrity to teeth's end—loyalty none more extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He kept faith to the grave—no loyalty purer.

sentences.zh: 而傾側顛沛，僅而自全，則伊生抱明允以嬰戮，文子懷忠敬而齒劍，固其所也。

translations.literal: Yet tilting and stumbling, barely self-preserving—then Yi Sheng embraced bright fairness yet encountered execution; Wenzi cherished loyalty and reverence yet met sword at teeth—solidly their lot.
translations.idiomatic: Still they staggered through ruin barely alive: Yi Yin wore integrity yet faced the headsman's blade; Wen Zhong served with devotion yet fell on his sword—small wonder.

sentences.zh: 因斯以言，夫以篤聖穆親，如彼之懿，大德至忠，如此之盛，尚不能取信於人主之懷，止謗於眾多之口，過此以往，惡睹其可！

translations.literal: By this to speak—using such sage-deep gentle kinship like that excellence, great virtue utmost loyalty like such flourishing—still unable to obtain trust in the lord of men's breast, stop slander in the multitude's mouths—passing this to go forth—how see its possibility!
translations.idiomatic: If kinship so honorable and loyalty so deep still failed to win the ruler's trust or silence gossip, what hope has anyone beyond them?

sentences.zh: 安危之理，斷可識矣。

translations.literal: The principle of safety and peril—decidedly can be known.
translations.idiomatic: The calculus of survival ought to be plain.

sentences.zh: 又況乎饕大名以冒道家之忌，運短才而易聖哲所難者哉！

translations.literal: How much more those who covet great names to risk Dao school's taboos, wield short talent yet exchange sage-wise men's difficulties!
translations.idiomatic: How much worse to chase grand fame against Heaven's warning, or wield shallow wit on puzzles that baffled the sages!

sentences.zh: 身危由於勢過，而不知去勢以求安；

translations.literal: Body peril arises from power exceeding, yet not knowing to discard power to seek peace;
translations.idiomatic: Peril comes when power swells past measure, yet men refuse to shed power to find peace;

sentences.zh: 禍積起于寵盛，而不知辭寵以招福。

translations.literal: calamity accumulates rising from favor flourishing, yet not knowing to decline favor to summon blessing.
translations.idiomatic: disaster gathers when favor crests, yet they will not reject favor to invite fortune.

sentences.zh: 見百姓之謀己，則申宮警守，以崇不畜之威；

translations.literal: Seeing the hundred surnames plot against himself, then extends palace and warns guard, thereby to elevate unrestrainable awe;
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting the people plot against them, they tighten palace guards and inflate a majesty no subject may endure;

sentences.zh: 懼萬方之不服，則嚴刑峻制，以賈傷心之怨。

translations.literal: fearing the myriad directions' non-submission, then severe punishments harsh controls, thereby to trade heartbreaking resentment.
translations.idiomatic: fearing every quarter might rebel, they pile cruel laws until hearts turn bitter.

sentences.zh: 然後威窮乎震主，而怨行乎上下，眾心日陊，危機將發，而方偃仰瞪眄，謂足以誇世，笑古人之未工，忘己事之已拙，知曩勳之可矜，暗成敗之有會。

translations.literal: Then awe exhausts in shaking the lord; resentment moves above and below; hosts of hearts daily decay; peril's pivot will erupt—yet just then leaning back staring sidelong, deeming sufficient to boast to the world, laughing ancients' lack of skill, forgetting own affairs' already clumsy, knowing former merit's boast-worthiness, blind to success-failure's having junction.
translations.idiomatic: Majesty tips into menace; resentment spreads high and low; loyalty frays by the day; crisis looms—yet they lounge about, sneering that they outshine antiquity, mocking forebears as clumsy, fondling old laurels while blind to how fortune turns.

sentences.zh: 是以事窮運盡，必有顛仆；

translations.literal: Therefore when affairs exhaust and fortune ends, there must be collapse;
translations.idiomatic: When luck runs out, the fall comes hard;

sentences.zh: 風起塵合，而禍至常酷也。

translations.literal: wind rises dust joins—and calamity's arrival is constantly cruel.
translations.idiomatic: storm winds whip dust into teeth, and ruin strikes without mercy.

sentences.zh: 聖人忌功名之過己，惡寵祿之逾量，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Sages taboo merit-fame's exceeding self; hate favor-salary's exceeding measure—generally for this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why sages shrink from fame beyond desert and stipends above measure.

sentences.zh: 夫惡欲之大端，賢愚所共有，而遊子殉高位于生前，志士思垂名於身後，受生之分，惟此而已。

translations.literal: The great ends of hate and desire, sage and fool share together; yet wandering sons martyr high rank before life; aspirant knights think to trail fame after body—received life's allotment, only this ends.
translations.idiomatic: Love and loathing rule sage and fool alike: some chase titles in life, others chase names beyond the grave—within our mortal portion, nothing else remains.

sentences.zh: 夫蓋世之業，名莫盛焉；

translations.literal: Now covering-the-age's enterprise—fame none more splendid;
translations.idiomatic: Empires overshadowing an age earn the loftiest fame;

sentences.zh: 率意無違，欲莫順焉。

translations.literal: Following intent without opposition—desire none more compliant.
translations.idiomatic: follow whim without check and every craving seems tame.

sentences.zh: 借使伊人頗覽天道，知盡不可益，盈難久持，超然自引，高揖而退，則巍巍之盛，仰邈前賢，洋洋之風，俯觀來籍，而大欲不止於身，至樂無愆乎舊，節彌效而德彌廣，身逾逸而名逾劭。

translations.literal: Suppose such men broadly viewed Heaven's way, knew fullness cannot be increased, surplus hard long to hold, transcendent self-withdrew, high bowed and retired—then lofty-lofty's flourishing, gaze distant former worthies; vast-vast's wind, look down coming records—and great desire not stop at body, utmost joy without fault toward old—restraint ever more effective yet virtue ever broader, body ever more leisurely yet name ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Had they read Heaven's pattern—seen that peaks cannot climb forever nor fullness endure—and stepped back with a bow, they might have matched ancient paragons above and left shining pages below. Desire would ease, joy stay blameless, virtue widen as they yielded, fame sharpen as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 此之不為，而彼之必昧，然後河海之跡堙為窮流，一匱之釁積成山嶽，名編凶頑之條，身厭荼毒之痛，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: This not doing, yet that must dim—then river-sea's traces blocked become exhausted streams; one basket's crack accumulates into hills and peaks; name compiled on vicious-stubborn rolls; body satiated with bitter-poison pain—is it not erroneous!
translations.idiomatic: Refusing this course, they rush blind into ruin—rivers shrink to ditches, small cracks yawn into chasms, their names land on traitors' lists, their bodies taste agony. Could folly run deeper?

sentences.zh: 故聊為賦焉，庶使百世少有悟雲。

translations.literal: Therefore casually I compose this rhapsody, hoping perhaps to make hundred generations slightly have awakening.
translations.idiomatic: I jot this rhapsody down, hoping a few souls centuries hence might wake.

sentences.zh: 冏不之悟，而竟以敗。

translations.literal: Jiong did not awaken to this, and in the end thereby failed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiong ignored the warning—and fell all the same.

sentences.zh: 機又以聖王經國，義在封建，因采其遠指，著《五等論》曰：

translations.literal: Ji further because sage kings ordering states, righteousness lay in enfeoffment, thereby adopting its far-reaching purport, composed Discourse on the Five Ranks saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji also argued that sagely kings ordered the realm through feudal allotments; gathering these deeper implications he wrote his Discourse on the Five Ranks:

sentences.zh: 夫體國經野，先王所慎，創制垂基，思隆後葉。

translations.literal: Embodying state and regulating wilds—former kings were cautious; founding institutions handing down foundations—thinking to enrich later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering capital and countryside demands utmost care: founders laid frameworks hoping prosperity would reach generations yet unborn.

sentences.zh: 然而經略不同，長世異術。

translations.literal: Yet strategic planning differs; long-age arts differ.
translations.idiomatic: Plans diverged, and so did the arts of endurance.

sentences.zh: 五等之制，始于黃、唐，郡縣之治，創于秦、漢，得失成敗，備在典謨，是以其詳可得而言。

translations.literal: The five-ranks system began at Huang and Tang; commandery-county governance originated at Qin and Han; gain-loss success-defeat, fully in canons and counsels—therefore its detail can be obtained and spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The five ranks trace to high antiquity; commanderies and counties arose under Qin and Han. Canon and commentary spell out every triumph and failure—enough to weigh both systems fairly.

sentences.zh: 夫王者知帝業至重，天下至廣。

translations.literal: The king knows emperor enterprise is utmost heavy; all-under-heaven is utmost broad.
translations.idiomatic: A king knows the imperial enterprise weighs heavier than anything and the realm stretches wider than sight.

sentences.zh: 廣不可以偏制，重不可以獨任。

translations.literal: Vastness cannot be lopsidedly controlled; weight cannot be solely borne.
translations.idiomatic: A realm too wide cannot be steered from one point; a burden too heavy cannot be carried alone.

sentences.zh: 任重必於借力，制廣終乎因人。

translations.literal: Heavy burden must borrow strength; broad control ends by relying on men.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy tasks demand borrowed strength; ruling vast lands ends by trusting others.

sentences.zh: 故設官分職，所以輕其任也；

translations.literal: Therefore establishing offices and dividing duties—thereby to lighten the burden;
translations.idiomatic: Hence offices multiply and duties divide—to lighten what rests on the throne;

sentences.zh: 並建伍長，所以弘其制也。

translations.literal: together establishing squad-leaders—thereby to enlarge its system.
translations.idiomatic: layer upon layer of local heads—to widen the system's reach.

sentences.zh: 於是乎立其封疆之典，裁其親疏之宜，使萬國相維，以成磐石之固；

translations.literal: Thereupon set their enclosure-boundary canons, trim closeness and distance's propriety, causing myriad states mutually to bind, thereby to complete foundation-stone solidity;
translations.idiomatic: They framed feudal boundaries and graded kin near and distant until myriad domains knitted together firm as bedrock;

sentences.zh: 宗庶雜居，而定維城之業。

translations.literal: kin by blood and by cadet branches mixed dwelling—and stabilizing city-wall-sustaining enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: kin and cadets mingled in each domain, locking every rampart to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又有以見綏世之長禦，識人情之大方，知其為人不如厚己，利物不如圖身；

translations.literal: Moreover thereby to see pacifying-age's long control, recognize human sentiment's great norm, knowing that benefiting others is not as good as enriching self; aiding things is not as good as plotting body;
translations.idiomatic: Here lay wise rule for an age: grasp human nature—others matter less than self, things profit less than one's skin;

sentences.zh: 安上在於悅下，為己存乎利人。

translations.literal: Pacifying superiors lies in pleasing inferiors; preserving self exists in benefiting others.
translations.idiomatic: secure the throne by pleasing those below; secure yourself by enriching others.

sentences.zh: 故《易》曰「悅以使人，人忘其勞」，孫卿曰「不利而利之，不如利而後利之利也」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says "with pleasure thereby employing men, men forget their toil"; Sun Qing says "not benefiting yet benefiting them is not as good as benefiting and afterward benefiting's benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says win hearts and labor feels light; Xunzi warns that profit seized without sharing trails profit freely shared.

sentences.zh: 是以分天下以厚樂，則己得與之同憂；

translations.literal: Therefore dividing all-under-heaven to enrich joy—then self obtains with them shared grief;
translations.idiomatic: Share the empire's bounty and you will share its sorrow;

sentences.zh: 饗天下以豐利，而己得與之共害。

translations.literal: feasting all-under-heaven with abundant profit—and self obtains with them shared harm.
translations.idiomatic: spread wealth abroad and harm will find you together.

sentences.zh: 利博而恩篤，樂遠則憂深，故諸侯享食土之實，萬國受傳世之祚。

translations.literal: Profit broad yet kindness thick; joy distant then grief deep—therefore feudal lords enjoy eating-soil's substance; myriad states receive handed-age's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Wide blessings deepen loyalty; distant joy breeds deep care—so lords truly tasted their soil's yield and lineages held mandate age after age.

sentences.zh: 夫然，則南面之君各務其政，九服之內知有定主，上之子愛於是乎生，下之禮信於是乎結，世平足以敦風，道衰足以禦暴。

translations.literal: Being thus, then south-facing lords each exert their governance; within nine garments know there is settled lord—above child-love thereby arises; below ritual-trust thereby binds; age peace suffices to enrich customs; way decay suffices to ward violence.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince minded his own realm; every province knew its sovereign; rulers nursed the people as children and subjects answered with faith—peace bred manners; decline still bred defenders.

sentences.zh: 故強毅之國不能擅一時之勢，雄俊之人無所寄霸王之志。

translations.literal: Therefore strong-resolute states cannot monopolize one moment's power; heroic outstanding men have nowhere to lodge hegemons' ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: No bold state could seize every advantage at once; no adventurer could vault alone to overlordship.

sentences.zh: 然後國安由萬邦之思化，主尊賴群後之圖身，譬猶眾目營方，則天網自昶；

translations.literal: Then state peace arises from myriad regions' thinking transformation; lord honor relies on host of marquises' plotting body—like many eyes managing directions, then Heaven's net itself expands;
translations.idiomatic: The throne rested on myriad districts pulling toward virtue; majesty rested on lords minding their skins—like countless eyes scanning corners until Heaven's net widened of itself;

sentences.zh: 四體辭難，而心膂獲乂。

translations.literal: four limbs resign difficulty—and heart and backbone obtain governance.
translations.idiomatic: limbs shrugged off peril while heart and spine stayed whole.

sentences.zh: 蓋三代所以直道，四王所以垂業也。

translations.literal: Generally the Three Ages' reason for straight way; the Four Kings' reason for handing enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the straight path of the Three Dynasties and the lasting work of the founding kings.

sentences.zh: 夫盛衰隆弊，理所固有，教之廢興，系乎其人，原法期於必諒，明道有時而暗。

translations.literal: Flourishing and waning, rise and decay—principle has them inherently; instruction's abolition and rise—ties to its men; tracing law aims at must-trust; clarifying the Way has times of darkness.
translations.idiomatic: Rise and fall are woven into order itself; rites live or die with the men who keep them. Law seeks steadfast truth; even the clearest Way knows nights of shadow.

sentences.zh: 故世及之制弊于強禦，厚下之典漏於末折，侵弱之釁遘自三委，陵夷之禍終乎七雄。

translations.literal: Therefore inheritance-by-age's system spoiled by strong oppression; thickening inferiors' canon leaked at end fracture; encroach-and-weakness's crack met from Three Lords yielding; gradual decline's calamity ended with Seven Heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary succession bred bullying ministers; favor to vassals frayed at the edges until nibbling aggression began with surrender after surrender and decay ran its course in the age of the Seven Powers.

sentences.zh: 昔成湯親照夏後之鑒，公旦目涉商人之戒，文質相濟，損益有物。

translations.literal: Formerly Cheng Tang personally illumined Xia successors' mirror; Duke Dan eye-crossed Shang men's warnings; pattern and substance mutually aided; diminish-increase had substance.
translations.idiomatic: Tang of Shang studied Xia's mirror; the Duke of Zhou walked Shang's caution—culture and simplicity balanced each shift.

sentences.zh: 然五等之禮，不革于時，封畛之制，有隆爾者，豈玩二王之禍而暗經世之算乎？

translations.literal: Yet five-ranks' ritual was not altered to the age; enclosure-boundary's system—had flourishing thus—could they toy at Two Kings' calamities yet blind to ordering-age's reckoning?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the five ranks stayed ritual kin to their age; border allotments still waxed or waned—were sages blind to later kings' ruin? Hardly; they counted generations ahead.

sentences.zh: 固知百世非可懸禦，善制不能無弊，而侵弱之辱愈於殄祀，土崩之困痛於陵夷也。

translations.literal: Solidly knowing hundred generations cannot be suspended-controlled; good systems cannot lack flaws—yet encroach-weakness's shame surpasses exterminated sacrifice; earth-collapse's hardship pains more than gradual decline.
translations.idiomatic: No institution lasts forever unguided; every good law ages—yet nibbling weakness hurts less than extinct temples; total collapse hurts worse than slow decay.

sentences.zh: 是以經始獲其多福，慮終取其少禍，非謂侯伯無可亂之符，郡縣非興化之具。

translations.literal: Therefore planning beginning obtains its many blessings; considering end selects its few calamities—not saying marquises and earls lack omens of disorder; commanderies and counties lack tools for raising transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Founders chose feudalism for maximal blessing and minimal ruin—not because lords cannot rebel or counties cannot civilize.

sentences.zh: 故國憂賴其釋位，主弱憑于翼戴。

translations.literal: Therefore state grief relied on their yielding rank; lord weakness depended on wing-canopy support.
translations.idiomatic: When peril struck, rulers leaned on lords who yielded power; weak sovereigns leaned on those who raised them up.

sentences.zh: 及承微積弊，王室遂卑，猶保名位，祚垂後嗣，皇統幽而不輟，神器否而必存者，豈非事勢使之然歟！

translations.literal: Coming to inheriting faint accumulating flaws, royal house became base—yet still preserving name-rank; blessing hung to posterity; imperial lineage dark yet unceasing; divine vessel obstructed yet must exist—is it not circumstance's power making it thus!
translations.idiomatic: Even when the house wore thin, titles endured, heirs continued, the thread never snapped—the tripod tarnished yet survived. Could mere geography explain it?

sentences.zh: 降及亡秦，棄道任術，懲周之失，自矜其得。

translations.literal: Descending to perished Qin, abandoned the Way and relied on method; punished Zhou's failure; self-praised its gains.
translations.idiomatic: Then came doomed Qin: it spurned moral sway for naked expedient, punishing Zhou's faults while congratulating itself.

sentences.zh: 尋斧始於所庇，制國昧於弱下，國慶獨饗其利，主憂莫與共害。

translations.literal: Soon axe began at what sheltered; controlling state darkened at weakening inferiors; national blessing alone enjoyed its profit; lord grief none shared harm.
translations.idiomatic: It swung the axe against its own shelter; it ruled blind to enfeebled subjects; it hoarded gain while its lord bore every grief alone.

sentences.zh: 雖速亡趨亂，不必一道，顛沛之釁，實由孤立。

translations.literal: Although swift death hastening disorder—need not one path—overturn-drench's crack truly arose from isolated standing.
translations.idiomatic: Paths to swift ruin vary; every collapse traced to standing utterly alone.

sentences.zh: 是蓋思五等之小怨，亡萬國之大德，知陵夷之可患，暗土崩之為痛也。

translations.literal: This generally thought five-ranks' small resentment, lost myriad states' great virtue; knew gradual decline's can be worried—dark to earth-collapse's being pain.
translations.idiomatic: They traded petty feudal quarrels for the broad virtue of many states; they feared gradual slide yet ignored catastrophic rupture.

sentences.zh: 周之不競，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Zhou's lack of contention—has come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's weakness had brewed long before.

sentences.zh: 國乏令主，十有餘世。

translations.literal: State lacked excellent lord—more than ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten reigns no worthy king sat the throne.

sentences.zh: 然片言勤王，諸侯必應，一朝振矜，遠國先叛，故強晉收其請隧之圖，暴楚頓其觀鼎之志，豈劉、項之能窺關，勝、廣之敢號澤哉！

translations.literal: Yet slice-word diligent king—feudal lords must respond; one morning shake pride—distant states first rebel—therefore strong Jin withdrew its request-tunnel plot; violent Chu halted its gaze-tripod ambition—how Liu and Xiang's ability to spy passes; Sheng and Guang's daring cry marshes!
