translations.idiomatic: Yet one call to rescue the throne rallied every lord; one hour of royal arrogance lost the frontier first—so Jin dropped its tunnel demand and Chu forgot the cauldrons. Was it Liu Bang who breached the passes or Chen Sheng who shouted from the marsh?

sentences.zh: 借使秦人因循其制，雖則無道，有與共亡，覆滅之禍，豈在曩日！

translations.literal: Suppose Qin men had followed along its system—even if lacking the Way—had with them shared perdition—overturn-extinction's calamity—would it have been in former days!
translations.idiomatic: Had Qin kept Zhou's feudal spine, even its cruelty would have met allies in ruin—would the throne have fallen so soon?

sentences.zh: 漢矯秦枉，大啟王侯，境土逾溢，不遵舊典，故賈生憂其危，晁錯痛其亂。

translations.literal: Han straightened Qin's crookedness, greatly opened kings and marquises, border lands overflowed excess, did not follow old canons—therefore Jia Sheng worried its peril; Chao Cuo ached its disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Han reversed Qin by flinging wide noble titles until domains spilled past precedent—hence Jia Yi's dread and Chao Cuo's alarm.

sentences.zh: 是以諸侯岨其國家之富，憑其士庶之力，勢足者反疾，土狹者逆遲，六臣犯其弱綱，七子沖其漏網，皇祖夷於黔徒，西京病於東帝。

translations.literal: Therefore feudal lords rugged their state's wealth, relied on their gentry-commoners' strength—power sufficient turned quickly; soil narrow rebelled slowly; six ministers violated its weak net; seven sons rushed its leaking net; august ancestor leveled among black laborers; western capital sickened by eastern emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lords fattened on wealth and militias—great domains revolted fast, tiny ones slow—until six ministers tore Han's thin laws, seven princes slipped the net, clans fell to common dust, and Chang'an bowed to eastern challengers.

sentences.zh: 是蓋過正之災，而非建侯之累也。

translations.literal: This generally excess-correcting's calamity—not establishing marquises' burden.
translations.idiomatic: That was excess correction, not feudalism's flaw.

sentences.zh: 然呂氏之難，朝士外顧；

translations.literal: Yet Lü clan's difficulty—court gentlemen looked outward;
translations.idiomatic: When the Lüs seized power, courtiers looked to the feudatories;

sentences.zh: 宋昌策漢，必稱諸侯。

translations.literal: Song Chang planned Han—must praise feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chang's counsel for Han named the lords first.

sentences.zh: 逮至中葉，忌其失節，割削宗子，有名無實，天下曠然，復襲亡秦之軌矣。

translations.literal: Coming down to middle leaf, envied their lost restraint, carved and shaved imperial sons—had name lacked substance; all-under-heaven emptily so—again inherited perished Qin's tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Han envied princely power and pared imperial sons to titles without troops—so the realm stood hollow and slid back toward Qin's lonely rail.

sentences.zh: 是以五侯作威，不忌萬國；

translations.literal: Therefore five marquises made awe—did not fear myriad states;
translations.idiomatic: Five court favorites strutted unafraid of any lord;

sentences.zh: 新都襲漢，易於拾遺也。

translations.literal: Xindu inherited Han—easy as picking lost objects.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang seized Han like snatching dropped coins.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，纂隆皇統，而由遵覆車之遺轍，養喪家之宿疾，僅及數世，奸宄棄斥。

translations.literal: Guangwu middle-rise, compiled eminent imperial lineage—yet by following overturned cart's leftover ruts, nourishing bereaved-house's chronic ailment—only reached several generations—wickedness cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu revived the Liu line yet drove the same rut that wrecked Qin, nursing old sickness—within a few reigns traitors filled the court.

sentences.zh: 卒有強臣專朝，則天下風靡，一夫從衡，而城池自夷，豈不危哉！

translations.literal: Finally had strong ministers monopolize court—then all-under-heaven wind-fell; one man followed balance—and city walls self-levelled—is it not perilous!
translations.idiomatic: Strong ministers soon owned the court; the realm bent like grass; one adventurer tipped the scale and walls fell without siege—was that safety?

sentences.zh: 在周之衰，難興王室，放命者七臣，幹位者三子，嗣王委其九鼎，凶族據其天邑，鉦鼙震於閫宇，鋒鏑流于絳闕，然禍止畿甸，害不覃及，天下晏然，以安待危。

translations.literal: In Zhou's decline, difficulty rose in royal house—license-givers seven ministers; interfere-position three sons; succeeding king entrusted his nine cauldrons; vicious clan occupied its heaven city; war-drums shook at gate-barrier; arrow-points flowed at crimson gate—yet calamity stopped at capital district; harm did not spread everywhere; all-under-heaven tranquil—used peace to await peril.
translations.idiomatic: Late Zhou saw seven officers spurn orders and three princes grasp rank—cauldrons slipped away, traitors held the capital, drums shook the gates and arrows flew at crimson towers—yet ruin stayed inside the plain while the realm waited calm.

sentences.zh: 是以宣王興于共和，襄惠振于晉、鄭。

translations.literal: Therefore King Xuan rose from Gonghe; Xiang and Hui revived from Jin and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan rose from joint rule; Kings Xiang and Hui rallied with Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 豈若二漢階闥暫擾，而四海已沸，嬖臣朝入，九服夕亂哉！

translations.literal: How like two Han's stair-door briefly disturbed—yet four seas already boiled; favorite ministers morning entered—nine garments evening disordered!
translations.idiomatic: Contrast Han: a brief palace scuffle boiled the seas—favorites slipped in at dawn and by dusk the empire burned.

sentences.zh: 遠惟王莽篡逆之事，近覽董卓擅權之際，億兆悼心，愚智同痛。

translations.literal: Far pondering Wang Mang usurp-rebellion's affairs; near perusing Dong Zhuo monopolize-power's moment—hundred-million grieved heart; fool and wise same pain.
translations.idiomatic: Remember Wang Mang's theft or watch Dong Zhuo's grip—every soul grieved, sage or fool alike.

sentences.zh: 然周以之存，漢以之亡，夫何故哉？

translations.literal: Yet Zhou by it survived; Han by it perished—what reason?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou survived such storms where Han died—why?

sentences.zh: 豈世乏曩時之臣，士無匡合之志歟？

translations.literal: Could age lack former times' ministers; gentlemen lack rectify-unite's ambition?
translations.idiomatic: Were good ministers fewer than before? Did ambition die?

sentences.zh: 蓋遠績屈于時異，雄心挫於卑勢耳。

translations.literal: Generally distant merit bends to age's difference; bold heart breaks at base position.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds bent before a changed age; bold hearts broke under petty circumstance.

sentences.zh: 故烈士扼腕，終委寇仇之手；

translations.literal: Therefore ardent knights grip wrists—finally entrust bandit-enemy's hands;
translations.idiomatic: Heroes gnashed wrists yet fell into bandit hands;

sentences.zh: 中人變節，以助虐國之桀。

translations.literal: middling men changed integrity—to aid cruel state's Jie.
translations.idiomatic: mediocre men switched sides and fed tyrants.

sentences.zh: 雖復時有鳩合同志以謀王室，然上非奧主，下皆市人，師旅無先定之班，君臣無相保之志，是以義兵雲合，無救劫殺之禍，眾望未改，而已見大漢之滅矣。

translations.literal: Although again times had dove-unite like-minded to plot royal house—yet above was not profound lord; below were all market men; armies lacked beforehand-fixed ranks; ruler-minister lacked mutual-preserve ambition—therefore righteous hosts cloud-joined—could not save robbery-killing's calamity; multitude expectation not yet changed—yet already saw great Han's extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes men rallied for the throne—but no worthy sovereign led them, troops were rabble without ranks, courtiers lacked mutual faith—so righteous armies gathered yet could not halt slaughter; hope lingered while Han already died.

sentences.zh: 或以「諸侯世位，不必常全，昏主暴君，有時比跡，故五等所以多亂。

translations.literal: Someone says "feudal lords' inherited positions—need not always be whole; dark lords violent tyrants—sometimes trace together—therefore five ranks' reason for much disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue hereditary lords breed corrupt rulers—hence chaos under feudal ranks.

sentences.zh: 今之牧守，皆官方庸能，雖或失之，其得固多，故郡縣易以為政」。

translations.literal: Today's shepherds and guards—all official-square commonplace ability—although perhaps losing it, their gains are solid many—therefore commanderies and counties easy to govern policy."
translations.idiomatic: Today's governors pass exams—failures happen, yet gains outweigh loss—so counties rule easier."

sentences.zh: 夫德之休明，黜陟日用，長率連屬，咸述其職，而淫昏之郡無所容過，何則其不治哉！

translations.literal: Virtue's splendid brightness—demotion-promotion daily used; long-leaders linked dependents—all narrate their duties—yet debauched-dark commanderies nowhere contain fault—why then their not governing!
translations.idiomatic: When virtue shines, promotions flow daily and every magistrate reports duty—could a vicious prefect hide? Why call that ungovernable?

sentences.zh: 故先代有以興矣。

translations.literal: Therefore former ages had thereby risen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties rose on such grounds.

sentences.zh: 苟或衰陵，百度自悖，鬻官之吏以貨准財，則貪殘之萌皆群後也，安在其不亂哉！

translations.literal: If perhaps decay mound—hundred measures self-perverse; selling-office clerks by goods gauge wealth—then greedy cruel's sprouts all group marquises—where lies their not disordering!
translations.idiomatic: But decay breeds contradiction—offices sell for silver—greed stains every lord alike. Where is peace then?

sentences.zh: 故後王有以之廢矣。

translations.literal: Therefore later kings had thereby abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Later kings abandoned such systems for cause.

sentences.zh: 且要而言之，五等之君，為己思政；

translations.literal: Moreover summarizing to speak—five-ranks' lords—for self think governance;
translations.idiomatic: In short, feudal lords mind their own realms;

sentences.zh: 郡縣之長，為吏圖物。

translations.literal: commanderies and counties' long—for clerk plot goods.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates scheme goods as hired clerks.

sentences.zh: 何以征之？

translations.literal: How to verify it?
translations.idiomatic: How know?

sentences.zh: 蓋企及進取，仕子之常志；

translations.literal: Generally striving-reach advance-seize—office-sons' constant intent;
translations.idiomatic: Ambition is every clerk's habit;

sentences.zh: 修己安人，良士所希及。

translations.literal: cultivate self pacify men—good knights' rare reach.
translations.idiomatic: self-cultivation and easing the people remain rare.

sentences.zh: 夫進取之情銳，而安人之譽遲，是故侵百姓以利己者，在位所不憚；

translations.literal: Advance-seize's sentiment sharp—yet pacify men's praise delayed—therefore encroach hundred surnames to profit self—those in position do not fear;
translations.idiomatic: Advancement rewards speed while kindness earns praise slowly—so magistrates strip commoners without qualm;

sentences.zh: 損實事以養名者，官長所夙慕也。

translations.literal: Harm solid affairs to nurture name—official longs' morning admired.
translations.idiomatic: they hollow real work to polish reputations they have coveted all along.

sentences.zh: 君無卒歲之圖，臣挾一時之志。

translations.literal: Lord lacks whole-year's plans; ministers clasp one moment's intents.
translations.idiomatic: The throne plans no further than the year; ministers chase the fashion of the hour.

sentences.zh: 五等則不然。

translations.literal: Five ranks then not so.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords differ.

sentences.zh: 知國為己土，眾皆我民；

translations.literal: Know state as own soil—multitudes all my people;
translations.idiomatic: They know the realm is private soil and every soul their charge;

sentences.zh: 民安，己受其利；

translations.literal: people peaceful—self receives its profit;
translations.idiomatic: when people thrive, they reap the yield;

sentences.zh: 國傷，家嬰其病。

translations.literal: state wounded—house infant its sickness.
translations.idiomatic: when the land bleeds, their own house sickens.

sentences.zh: 故前人欲以垂後，後嗣思其堂構，為上無苟且之心，群下知膠固之義。

translations.literal: Therefore former men wished thereby to hang to later; later heirs think their hall-frame—above no careless heart; groups below know glue-solid meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Forebears built for heirs who cherish ancestral beams—lords scorn shortcuts; followers grasp loyalty like lacquer.

sentences.zh: 使其並賢居政，則功有厚薄；

translations.literal: Suppose them together worthy dwelling governance—then merit has thick thin;
translations.idiomatic: When multiple worthy lords rule, deeds differ in weight;

sentences.zh: 兩愚處亂，則過有深淺。

translations.literal: two fools dwell disorder—then fault has deep shallow.
translations.idiomatic: when two foolish lords reign error ranges shallow or deep.

sentences.zh: 然則八代之制，幾可以一理貫；

translations.literal: Being so—then eight generations' systems—nearly can one principle thread;
translations.idiomatic: Eight dynasties of feudal rule thus speak one logic;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢之典，殆可以一言蔽也。

translations.literal: Qin and Han's canons—almost can one phrase cover.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han county rule sums in a single sentence.

sentences.zh: 時成都王穎推功不居，勞謙下士。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Chengdu Ying pushed merit without occupying, toiled humble below gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chengdu refused credit and humbled himself before scholars.

sentences.zh: 機既感全濟之恩，又見朝廷屢有變難，謂穎必能康隆晉室，遂委身焉。

translations.literal: Ji already grateful for whole-save grace, again saw court repeatedly had changes calamities—thought Ying must can healthy prosper Jin house—thereupon entrusted body thereto.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji owed him his life and watched the court reel—he believed Ying could restore Jin and pledged himself wholly.

sentences.zh: 穎以機參大將軍軍事，表為平原內史。

translations.literal: Ying used Ji to participate in Grand General military affairs; memorialized him as Plain Interior Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ying named him army adviser to the grand general and recommended him interior secretary of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太安初，穎與河間王顒起兵討長沙王乂，假機後將軍、河北大都督，督北中郎將王粹、冠軍牽秀等諸軍二十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Early Taian, Ying with Prince Hejian Yong raised troops to punish Prince Changsha Yi—borrowed Ji Rear General, Hebei Grand Commander—supervised North Palace General Wang Cui, Champion Qian Xiu and such hosts over two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taian Ying joined Prince Yong of Hejian against Prince Yi of Changsha, naming Lu Ji rear general and commander-in-chief north of the Yellow River over Wang Cui, Qian Xiu, and more than two hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 機以三世為將，道家所忌，又羈旅入宦，屯居群士之右，而王粹、牽秀等皆有怨心，固辭都督。

translations.literal: Ji because three generations were generals—Dao school taboos—again sojourner entered office, stationed dwelling above host of gentlemen—yet Wang Cui, Qian Xiu and such all had resentful hearts—firmly declined commander.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji cited the proverb against three generations of generals, his outsider status, and resentment from Wang Cui and Qian Xiu—he firmly refused command.

sentences.zh: 穎不許。

translations.literal: Ying did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying refused his refusal.

sentences.zh: 機鄉人孫惠亦勸機讓都督于粹，機曰：「將謂吾為首鼠避賊，適所以速禍也。

translations.literal: Ji's townsman Sun Hui also urged Ji yield commander to Cui—Ji said: "They will say I am head-mouse avoiding bandits—precisely thereby hasten calamity."
translations.idiomatic: His townsman Sun Hui urged him to yield command to Wang Cui. Lu Ji replied, "They would call me a coward shirking battle—that would only hasten disaster."

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: Thereupon proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: He marched.

sentences.zh: 穎謂機曰：「若功成事定，當爵為郡公，位以台司，將軍勉之矣！

translations.literal: Ying told Ji: "If merit completes affair settles—then ennoble as commandery duke, rank with terrace ministers—General exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Ying told him, "When this is done I will make you a duke and minister of state—do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 」機曰：「昔齊桓任夷吾以建九合之功，燕惠疑樂毅以失垂成之業，今日之事，在公不在機也。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Formerly Qi Huan employed Yiwu thereby to establish nine-convergence's merit; Yan Hui doubted Yue Yi thereby to lose nearly-complete enterprise—today's affair lies in lord not in Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji answered, "Duke Huan trusted Guan Zhong and united the state; King Hui of Yan doubted Yue Yi and ruined a victory almost won—today hangs on you, not on me."

sentences.zh: 」穎左長史盧志心害機寵，言於穎曰：「陸機自比管、樂，擬君暗主，自古命將遣師，未有臣陵其君而可以濟事者也。

translations.literal: Ying's left chief clerk Lu Zhi heart harmed Ji's favor—spoke to Ying saying: "Lu Ji self-compares Guan, Le—likens lord dark lord—from antiquity ordering generals dispatching armies—never has minister override his lord yet can complete affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, chief clerk, envied Lu Ji and murmured to Ying, "Lu Ji ranks himself with Guan Zhong and Yue Yi and casts you as a blind ruler—since when did subjects bully kings and still succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」穎默然。

translations.literal: Ying fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Ying said nothing.

sentences.zh: 機始臨戎，而牙旗折，意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Ji first approached weapons—yet fang-banner snapped—intent greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: As Lu Ji first took the field his banner pole snapped—a grim omen.

sentences.zh: 列軍自朝歌至於河橋，鼓聲聞數百里，漢、魏以來，出師之盛，未嘗有也。

translations.literal: Arrayed armies from Zhaoge reaching River Bridge—drum sounds heard several hundred li—since Han and Wei—expedition hosts' splendor—never had there been.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts stretched from Zhaoge to the Yellow River bridge—drums rolled for hundreds of li—the greatest mobilization since Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂奉天子與機戰于鹿苑，機軍大敗，赴七里澗而死者如積焉，水為之不流，將軍賈棱皆死之。

translations.literal: Prince Changsha Yi upheld Son of Heaven with Ji battled at Deer Park—Ji's army greatly defeated—those who rushed Seven-li Stream and died were like piled—water by this did not flow—General Jia Ling both died therein.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Changsha led the emperor against Lu Ji at Deer Park; Lu Ji's army broke. Corpses dammed the Seven-li gorge till the water stalled—General Jia Ling died among them.

sentences.zh: 初，宦人孟玖弟超並為穎所嬖寵。

translations.literal: Formerly eunuch Meng Jiu's younger brother Chao together were by Ying favored.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Meng Jiu and his brother Meng Chao had both been Ying's favorites.

sentences.zh: 超領萬人為小都督，未戰，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: Chao led ten thousand men as petty commander—before battle—released troops greatly plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chao led ten thousand as sub-commander and looted wildly before the battle.

sentences.zh: 機錄其主者。

translations.literal: Ji recorded its chief men.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji arrested the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 超將鐵騎百餘人，直入機麾下奪之，顧謂機曰：「貉奴能作督不！

translations.literal: Chao led iron cavalry hundred-some men—straight entered Ji's banner-under seized them—turned telling Ji saying: "Badger-slave can act commander or not!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chao burst into headquarters with a hundred riders, snatched them back, and sneered, "Can a raccoon-dog pretend to command?"

sentences.zh: 」機司馬孫拯勸機殺之，機不能用。

translations.literal: Ji's Major Sun Zheng urged Ji kill him—Ji could not employ.
translations.idiomatic: Major Sun Zheng urged Lu Ji to execute him; Lu Ji refused.

sentences.zh: 超宣言於眾曰：「陸機將反。

translations.literal: Chao declared speech to host saying: "Lu Ji will rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chao publicly accused Lu Ji of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」又還書與玖言機持兩端，軍不速決。

translations.literal: Again returned letter with Jiu speaking Ji holds two ends—army not speedy decide.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his brother that Lu Ji hesitated between sides and stalled battle.

sentences.zh: 及戰，超不受機節度，輕兵獨進而沒。

translations.literal: When battle—Chao did not receive Ji's regulation—light troops alone advanced and perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fight Meng Chao disobeyed Lu Ji, charged ahead with light troops, and died.

sentences.zh: 玖疑機殺之，遂譖機於穎，言其有異志。

translations.literal: Jiu suspected Ji killed him—thereupon slandered Ji to Ying—speaking he had different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu suspected Lu Ji of murder and slandered him to Ying as disloyal.

sentences.zh: 將軍王闡、郝昌、公師籓等皆玖所用，與牽秀等共證之。

translations.literal: Generals Wang Chan, Hao Chang, Gongshi Fan and such were all men Jiu employed; together with Qian Xiu and others they jointly testified against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chan, Hao Chang, Gongshi Fan—Meng Jiu's creatures—joined Qian Xiu to bear false witness.

sentences.zh: 穎大怒，使秀密收機。

translations.literal: Ying greatly raged and ordered Qian Xiu secretly seize Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Ying told Qian Xiu to arrest Lu Ji by stealth.

sentences.zh: 其夕，機夢黑幰繞車，手決不開，天明而秀兵至。

translations.literal: That night Ji dreamed black carriage-curtains wound his cart; his hands could not tear them open—at dawn Qian Xiu's soldiers arrived.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lu Ji dreamed dark drapes choking his carriage—he could not tear free—and at daybreak Qian Xiu's men came.

sentences.zh: 機釋戎服，著白帢，與秀相見，神色自若，謂秀曰：「自吳朝傾覆，吾兄弟宗族蒙國重恩，入侍帷幄，出剖符竹。

translations.literal: Ji shed martial dress and put on white kerchief cap; meeting Qian Xiu his spirit remained composed—he told Qian Xiu: "Since Wu court overturned, my brothers and clan received state's heavy grace—entered serving curtain strategy, went out carving tally bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: He doffed armor for a plain white cap and faced Qian Xiu calmly. "After Wu fell," he said, "my kin owed Jin everything—counsel within the curtain, command beyond with tally in hand."

sentences.zh: 成都命吾以重任，辭不獲已。

translations.literal: Chengdu ordered me with heavy duty—I declined but could not obtain stop.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Chengdu pressed a grave charge on me until refusal was impossible.

sentences.zh: 今日受誅，豈非命也！

translations.literal: Today receiving execution—is it not fate!
translations.idiomatic: To die today—is that not fate itself?"

sentences.zh: 」因與穎箋，詞甚淒惻。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Ying he wrote a note—words extremely mournful.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Ying a letter heartbreakingly earnest.

sentences.zh: 既而歎曰：「華亭鶴唳，豈可復聞乎！

translations.literal: Then sighing said: "Huating cranes' cry—how can it be heard again!
translations.idiomatic: Then he sighed, "Shall I ever hear the cranes of Huating again?"

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害於軍中，時年四十三。

translations.literal: Thereupon met harm in the army—aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: They cut him down in camp. He was forty-three.

sentences.zh: 二子蔚、夏亦同被害。

translations.literal: Two sons Wei and Xia likewise together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lu Wei and Lu Xia died with him.

sentences.zh: 機既死非其罪，士卒痛之，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Ji having died not his crime, soldiers grieved him—none did not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji died innocent; the ranks wept until none had dry cheeks.

sentences.zh: 是日昏霧晝合，大風折木，平地尺雪，議者以為陸氏之冤。

translations.literal: That day dusk fog noon merged; great wind snapped trees; flat ground foot-deep snow—discussers deemed it Lu clan's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: That noon fog swallowed daylight; gales snapped trees; snow a foot deep on level ground—onlookers called it heaven's proof of the Lu family's wrong.

sentences.zh: 機天才秀逸，辭藻宏麗，張華嘗謂之曰：「人之為文，常恨才少，而子更患其多。

translations.literal: Ji's heavenly talent elegant drifting; phrase-carving vast splendid—Zhang Hua once told him saying: "Men composing writing—always resent talent little—yet you further worry its abundance."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's genius flowed effortless; his lines blazed—Zhang Hua once said, "Writers usually mourn scarce talent—only you fret having too much."

sentences.zh: 」弟雲嘗與書曰：「君苗見兄文，輒欲燒其筆硯。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yun once wrote letter saying: "Junmiao seeing elder brother's writing—then wished burn his brush inkstone."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun wrote, "When Junmiao reads your prose he wants to burn brush and inkstone."

sentences.zh: 」後葛洪著書，稱「機文猶玄圃之積玉，無非夜光焉，五河之吐流，泉源如一焉。

translations.literal: Later Ge Hong composed book praising "Ji's writing is like Dark Garden's piled jade—none not night radiance; Five Rivers' vomiting flow—spring sources alike."
translations.idiomatic: Later Ge Hong wrote that Lu Ji's prose was piled jade from the Kunlun gardens—every piece a pearl—or five rivers pouring from one springhead.

sentences.zh: 其弘麗妍贍，英銳漂逸，亦一代之絕乎！

translations.literal: Its vast splendid beauty keen sharp drifting ease—also one generation's utmost!
translations.idiomatic: Grand, lush, keen, and free—peerless in an age!"

sentences.zh: 」其為人所推服如此。

translations.literal: Such men pushed and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The world esteemed him at that level.

sentences.zh: 然好游權門，與賈謐親善，以進趣獲譏。

translations.literal: Yet loved roaming power gates—was intimate with Jia Mi—by advancement zeal gained ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he haunted great houses and flattered Jia Mi—critics sneered at his ambition.

sentences.zh: 所著文章凡三百餘篇，並行於世。

translations.literal: Composed writings altogether three hundred-some pieces—all circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His writings ran past three hundred pieces and circulated everywhere.

sentences.zh: 孫拯者，字顯世，吳都富春人也。

translations.literal: Sun Zheng, courtesy name Xianshi, was a man of Wu capital Fuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zheng, courtesy Xianshi, came from Fuchun in the Wu metropolitan commandery.

sentences.zh: 能屬文，仕吳為黃門郎。

translations.literal: Could compose writing—served Wu as Palace Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well and served Wu as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孫皓世，侍臣多得罪，惟拯與顧榮以智全。

translations.literal: Sun Hao age—attendant ministers many got offense—only Zheng with Gu Rong by wisdom preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao many courtiers fell—only Sun Zheng and Gu Rong kept their wits and survived.

sentences.zh: 吳平後，為涿令，有稱績。

translations.literal: After Wu pacified—became Zhuo county magistrate—had praised traces.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he became magistrate of Zhuo county with a praised record.

sentences.zh: 機既為孟玖等所誣收拯考掠，兩踝骨見，終不變辭。

translations.literal: Ji having been by Meng Jiu and others slandered—seized Zheng and examined flogging—both ankle bones showed—finally did not change testimony.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji fell to Meng Jiu's plot they seized Sun Zheng and tortured him until his ankle bones showed—he never changed his story.

sentences.zh: 門生費慈、宰意二人詣獄明拯，拯譬遣之曰：「吾義不可誣枉知故，卿何宜復爾？

translations.literal: Disciples Fei Ci and Zai Yi two men went to prison clarifying Zheng—Zheng metaphorically sent them saying: "My righteousness cannot slander wrong old acquaintance—you why should again thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Students Fei Ci and Zai Yi pled his case in jail; Sun Zheng sent them away: "I cannot frame an old friend—why torment yourselves for me?"

sentences.zh: 」二人曰：「僕亦安得負君！

translations.literal: Two men said: "Servants also how can betray lord!
translations.idiomatic: "How could we betray you?"

sentences.zh: 」拯遂死獄中，而慈、意亦死。

translations.literal: Zheng thereupon died in prison—yet Ci, Yi also died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zheng died in prison; Fei Ci and Zai Yi died as well.

sentences.zh: 雲字士龍，六歲能屬文，性清正，有才理。

translations.literal: Yun courtesy name Shilong—at six could compose writing—nature pure upright—had talent pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun, courtesy Shilong, composed essays at six—upright and lucid in judgment.

sentences.zh: 少與兄機齊名，雖文章不及機，而持論過之，號曰「二陸」。

translations.literal: Youth with elder brother Ji equal fame—although writing did not reach Ji—yet held discourse surpassed him—styled "Two Lu."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he rivaled Lu Ji in fame; his prose fell short, debate surpassed—together they were the Two Lu.

sentences.zh: 幼時吳尚書廣陵閔鴻見而奇之，曰：「此兒若非龍駒，當是鳳雛。

translations.literal: Young age Wu Minister Guangling Min Hong saw and wondered at him—said: "This child if not dragon colt—must be phoenix chick."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Minister Min Hong of Guangling marveled: "Either a dragon foal or a phoenix chick."

sentences.zh: 」後舉雲賢良，時年十六。

translations.literal: Later recommended Yun Worthy and Good—then age sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was recommended Worthy and Good.

sentences.zh: 吳平，入洛。

translations.literal: Wu pacified—entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 機初詣張華，華問云何在。

translations.literal: Ji first visited Zhang Hua—Hua asked where was he.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji first called on Zhang Hua, Zhang asked where his brother was.

sentences.zh: 機曰：「雲有笑疾，未敢自見。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Yun has laughing illness—did not dare self-present."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji said, "He has fits of laughter and feared to meet you unprepared."

sentences.zh: 」俄而雲至。

translations.literal: Shortly Yun arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu Yun arrived.

sentences.zh: 華為人多姿制，又好帛繩纏須。

translations.literal: Hua as man many postures systems—also loved silk rope winding beard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua cut a striking figure and tied his beard up with silk cord.

sentences.zh: 雲見而大笑，不能自已。

translations.literal: Yun seeing greatly laughed—could not self-stop.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun took one look and laughed uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 先是，嘗著縗絰上船，于水中顧見其影，因大笑落水，人救獲免。

translations.literal: Before this—once wore mourning cords boarding boat—in water looked back seeing his shadow—thereupon big laughed fell water—men rescued obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: Once in mourning garb he boarded a boat, glimpsed his reflection, laughed until he fell overboard—someone fished him out.

sentences.zh: 雲與荀隱素未相識，嘗會華坐，華曰：「今日相遇，可勿為常談。

translations.literal: Yun with Xun Yin plain never mutually knew—once met at Hua's seat—Hua said: "Today meeting—can not be common talk."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun and Xun Yin had never met. At Zhang Hua's salon Zhang said, "Meet as strangers—skip the usual pleasantries."

sentences.zh: 」雲因抗手曰：「雲間陸士龍。

translations.literal: Yun thereupon raised hand saying: "Between-clouds Lu Shilong."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun raised his cup: "Lu Shilong from Between the Clouds."

sentences.zh: 」隱曰：「日下荀鳴鶴。

translations.literal: Yin said: "Under-sun Xun Minghe."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yin answered, "Xun Minghe from Beneath the Sun."

sentences.zh: 」鳴鶴，隱字也。

translations.literal: Minghe—Yin's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Minghe was Xun Yin's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 雲又曰：「既開青雲睹白雉，何不張爾弓，挾爾矢？

translations.literal: Yun again said: "Already opened green clouds seeing white pheasant—why not draw your bow—clamp your arrows?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun pressed, "Green clouds parted and showed a white pheasant—why not bend your bow and nock an arrow?"

sentences.zh: 」隱曰：「本謂是雲龍騤騤，乃是山鹿野麋。

translations.literal: Yin said: "Originally thought was cloud-dragon kui kui—actually mountain deer wild elk.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yin replied, "I expected a cloud dragon stalking proud—a hill elk or marsh deer instead."

sentences.zh: 獸微弩強，是以發遲。

translations.literal: Beast slight crossbow strong—therefore release delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The quarry looks small but your bow is stout—so my shot comes late."

sentences.zh: 」華撫手大笑。

translations.literal: Hua stroked hand greatly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua clapped his knees and roared.

sentences.zh: 刺史周浚召為從事，謂人曰：「陸士龍當今之顏子也。」

translations.literal: Inspector Zhou Jun summoned as attendant—told men saying: "Lu Shilong is today's Yan Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhou Jun made him clerk and said, "Lu Shilong is our age's Yan Hui."

sentences.zh: 俄以公府掾為太子舍人，出補浚儀令。

translations.literal: Shortly by public office aide became Crown Prince attendant—went out supplemented Junyi county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose from aide in the great minister's office to crown prince attendant, then magistrate of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 縣居都會之要，名為難理。

translations.literal: County dwelt capital-meeting's vital—named difficult to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Junyi sat at a capital junction—famous as hard to rule.

sentences.zh: 雲到官肅然，下不能欺，市無二價。

translations.literal: Yun arrived office solemn—inferiors could not deceive—market had no second price.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun ran a stern court—clerks dared not cheat—markets showed a single fair price.

sentences.zh: 人有見殺者，主名不立，雲錄其妻，而無所問。

translations.literal: Someone had seen killed person—chief name not established—Yun recorded his wife—yet asked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: A murder lacked a principal suspect; Lu Yun took the widow into custody yet questioned no one.

sentences.zh: 十許日遣出，密令人隨後，謂曰：「其去不出十里，當有男子候之與語，便縛來。

translations.literal: Ten-some days dismissed her—secretly ordered man follow after—telling saying: "Her leaving not beyond ten li—should have man await her speaking—then bind bring."
translations.idiomatic: After ten days he released her and secretly had men tail her: "Within ten li some man will stop her to speak—seize him."

sentences.zh: 」既而果然。

translations.literal: Shortly indeed thus.
translations.idiomatic: It happened exactly so.

sentences.zh: 問之具服，云：「與此妻通，共殺其夫，聞妻得出，欲與語，憚近縣，故遠相要候。

translations.literal: Questioned him fully confessed—saying: "With this wife adulterated—together killed her husband—heard wife could exit—wished speak with her—feared near county—therefore far arranged await."
translations.idiomatic: Under questioning he confessed: "I slept with her and helped kill her husband; when I heard she was freed I meant to meet her but feared the county seat, so I waited far out."

sentences.zh: 」於是一縣稱其神明。

translations.literal: Thereupon one county praised his spirit clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The whole county called him uncanny.

sentences.zh: 郡守害其能，屢譴責之，雲乃去官。

translations.literal: Commandery guardian harmed his ability—repeatedly censured blamed him—Yun thereupon left office.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect envied him and berated him repeatedly—Lu Yun resigned.

sentences.zh: 百姓追思之，圖畫形象，配食縣社。

translations.literal: Hundred surnames pursued thought him—drew painted images—paired sacrifice county soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: People missed him—set portraits beside the county god.

sentences.zh: 尋拜吳王晏郎中令。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Prince Wu Yan palace superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Yan of Wu named him superintendent of his household.

sentences.zh: 晏于西園大營第室，雲上書曰：

translations.literal: Yan at West Garden greatly built mansion chambers—Yun submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan lavished funds on mansions in the Western Garden—Lu Yun memorialized:

sentences.zh: 時晏信任部將，使覆察諸官錢帛，雲又陳曰：

translations.literal: At time Yan trusted deputy generals—made audit inspect various offices' coin silk—Yun again stated saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince then tasked brigade officers with auditing office accounts—Lu Yun protested again:

sentences.zh: 伏見令書，以部曲將李咸、馮南、司馬吳定、給使徐泰等覆校諸官市買錢帛簿。

translations.literal: I humbly see directive letter—using brigade generals Li Xian, Feng Nan, Major Wu Ding, attendant Xu Tai and such re-audit various offices market-buy coin silk registers.
translations.idiomatic: Your directive orders Brigade Commander Li Xian, Feng Nan, Major Wu Ding, and attendant Xu Tai to re-check every office purchase ledger.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以聖德龍興，光有大國，選眾官材，庶工肄業。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks sagely virtue dragon rises—lightens great state—selects crowd officers' timber—myriad craftsmen pursue enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes Your Highness's dragon ascent lights a great kingdom—you chose officers for timber and trained artisans for duty.

sentences.zh: 中尉該、大農誕皆清廉淑慎，恪居所司，其下眾官，悉州閭一介，疏暗之咎，雖可日聞，至於處義用情，庶無大戾。

translations.literal: Captain Gai and Minister of Agriculture Dan are both pure honest cautious careful—respectfully dwell in what they oversee—the host of officials beneath—all village lane single fellows—coarse-dark faults—although can daily heard—as for dwelling righteousness employing affection—probably without great violation.
translations.idiomatic: Captain of the Guard Gai and Minister of Agriculture Dan are scrupulous men anchored in their posts; subordinates are humble locals whose petty slips surface daily, yet in justice and tact they commit no grave offense.

sentences.zh: 今咸、南軍旅小人，定、泰士卒廝賤，非有清慎素著，忠公足稱。

translations.literal: Now Xian, Nan army-travel petty men—Ding, Tai soldier-attendant base mean—not having pure cautious plain renown—loyal public worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and Feng Nan are camp henchmen; Wu Ding and Xu Tai are low-order troop attendants—neither famed for integrity nor proved loyal.

sentences.zh: 大臣所關，猶謂未詳，咸等督察，然後得信，既非開國勿用之義，又傷殿下推誠曠蕩之量。

translations.literal: Great ministers' concern—still deemed not detailed—Xian and others supervise inspect—then afterward obtain trust—already not founding state's "do not use" meaning—again wounds Your Highness push sincerity vast breadth's measure.
translations.idiomatic: Weighty affairs barely earn scrutiny—yet these men "verify" truth; this flouts the founders' ban on misused agents and bruises your reputation for open trust.

sentences.zh: 雖使咸等能盡節益國，而功利百倍，至於光輔國美，猶未若開懷信士之無失。

translations.literal: Although suppose Xian and others able exhaust utmost benefit state—yet merit-profit hundred times—as for lighting aiding state's beauty—still not like opening bosom trusting gentlemen's lack of fault.
translations.idiomatic: Even were they to prove loyal beyond measure and profit the realm a hundredfold, they could not match the glory of trusting worthy men without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 況所益不過姑息之利，而使小人用事，大道陵替，此臣所以慷慨也。

translations.literal: Moreover what benefit is no more than indulgent profit—yet makes petty men wield affairs—great course gradual decay—this your servant's reason for generous indignation.
translations.idiomatic: The gain is petty tolerance at best while petty men steer policy—this is why your servant burns with grief.

sentences.zh: 臣備位大臣，職在獻可，苟有管見，敢不盡規。

translations.literal: Your servant occupies minister's place—duty lies presenting acceptable—if have tube-view—dare not exhaust regulation.
translations.idiomatic: I stand among great officers charged with candid counsel—how dare I hold back what little I see?

sentences.zh: 愚以宜發明令，罷此等覆察，眾事一付治書，則大信臨下，人思盡節矣。

translations.literal: Foolishly think should issue bright order—abolish such re-audits—crowd affairs altogether entrust Director of Documents—then great trust overlooks inferiors—men think exhaust fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict ending these audits and leave matters to the Director of Documents—great trust will reach below and men will give their utmost.

sentences.zh: 雲愛才好士，多所貢達。

translations.literal: Yun loved talent esteemed knights—many recommended promote reach.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun loved talent and raised many men.

sentences.zh: 移書太常府薦同郡張贍曰：

translations.literal: Sent letter Grand Chamberlain office recommending same commandery Zhang Shan saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Chamberlain recommending Zhang Shan of their commandery:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞在昔聖王，承天禦世，殷薦明德，思和人神，莫不崇典謨以教思，興禮學以陶遠。

translations.literal: I have heard in ancient sagely kings—upheld Heaven ordering age—deeply presented bright virtue—thought harmonize human spirits—none did not honor canons counsels to teach reflection—raise ritual learning to mold distance.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings who ruled by Heaven spread luminous virtue to harmonize gods and men—always teaching through canon and ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以帝堯昭煥而道協人天，西伯質文而周隆二代。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Yao brilliant splendid yet Way harmonized human Heaven—Western Earl substance pattern yet Zhou flourished two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus bright Yao aligned heaven and man; the Earl of the West balanced pattern and culture so Zhou rose through two ages.

sentences.zh: 大晉建皇，崇配天地，區夏既混，禮樂將庸。

translations.literal: Great Jin establishes emperor—honors pair Heaven Earth—inner summer already merged—ritual music about employ.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin seats its sovereign beside Heaven and earth; the realm is one—ritual and music wait deployment.

sentences.zh: 君侯應曆運之會，贊天人之期，博延俊茂，熙隆載典。

translations.literal: Lord marquise responds calendar-fortune's meeting—assists Heaven-human's term—broadly extends outstanding lush—glorious uplift carries canon.
translations.idiomatic: You ride the hour of destiny and aid Heaven's covenant—gather brilliance and lift the canon.

sentences.zh: 伏見衛將軍舍人同郡張贍，茂德清粹，器思深通。

translations.literal: I humbly see Guard General attendant same commandery Zhang Shan—lush virtue pure essence—vessel thought deep penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant presents Zhang Shan of your commandery, steward to the Guard General—virtue pure, judgment deep.

sentences.zh: 初慕聖門，棲心重仞，啟塗及階，遂升樞奧。

translations.literal: First admired sagely gate—nested heart heavy ren—opened path reaching steps—thereupon ascended pivot depth.
translations.idiomatic: He long sought the sage's school, climbed the high stair, and entered the inner chamber of learning.

sentences.zh: 抽靈匱于秘宮，披金滕于玄夏，思樂百氏，博采其珍；

translations.literal: Drew spirit-casket from secret palace—unfolded metal binders from dark summer—thought joy hundred clans—broadly gathered their treasures;
translations.idiomatic: He drew classics from the imperial treasury and opened metal-bound archives—took joy in every school and gathered their gems;

sentences.zh: 辭邁翰林，言敷其藻。

translations.literal: Phrasing surpasses brush-forest—speech spreads its algae.
translations.idiomatic: his phrases outshine the Hanlin forests—his words scatter ornament.

sentences.zh: 探微集逸，思心洞神；

translations.literal: Plucked subtle gathered stray—thought heart penetrates spirit;
translations.idiomatic: He probes the subtle and nets the overlooked—thought pierces to the spirit;

sentences.zh: 論道屬書，篇章光覿。

translations.literal: Discussed Way composed writings—chapters pieces light appeared.
translations.idiomatic: his essays on the Way shine when read.

sentences.zh: 含奇宰府，婆娑公門。

translations.literal: Held wonder steward office—pace sway public gate.
translations.idiomatic: He bears rare gifts in the minister's bureau—moves with ease at your gate.

sentences.zh: 棲靜隱寶，淪虛藏器；

translations.literal: Roost quiet hidden treasure—sink void concealing vessel;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he rests quiet as hidden treasure—depths that conceal a vessel;

sentences.zh: 褧裳襲錦，緇衣被玉。

translations.literal: Single garment layered brocade—black robe draped jade.
translations.idiomatic: he wears hemp over brocade—black silk over jade.

sentences.zh: 曾泉改路，懸車將邁，考盤下位，歲聿屢遷。

translations.literal: Zeng spring changed road—suspended carriage about depart—Kao Pan lower rank—year swiftly repeatedly shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Like water rerouted or a cart about to halt—he lingers in low office while years slip past.

sentences.zh: 搢紳之士，具懷愾恨。

translations.literal: Belt-gentry gentlemen—all cherish indignant regret.
translations.idiomatic: Every belted scholar burns with regret.

sentences.zh: 方今太清辟宇，四門啟籥，玄綱括地，天網廣羅；

translations.literal: Just now Grand Clarity opens vault—four gates open bolt—dark net spans earth—Heaven net broadly nets;
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand Clarity opens space; the four gates unlock; the dark net spans earth and heaven's net casts wide;

sentences.zh: 慶雲興以招龍，和風起而儀鳳，誠岩穴耀穎之秋，河津托乘之日也。

translations.literal: Auspicious clouds rise to summon dragons—harmonious winds rise and pattern phoenix—truly cliff cave shine ear autumn—river ford entrust ride day.
translations.idiomatic: auspicious clouds call dragons and mild winds measure phoenix—this is the season for recluses to gleam and scholars to board the raft.

sentences.zh: 而贍沈淪下位，群望悼心。

translations.literal: Yet Shan sinks submerged lower rank—crowd expectation grieves heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Shan still wallows in low rank—the hopeful mourn.

sentences.zh: 若得端委太學，錯綜先典；

translations.literal: If obtain spreading robes Grand Study—interweave warp ancient canons;
translations.idiomatic: Seat him in the academy to weave the classics;

sentences.zh: 垂纓玉階，論道紫宮，誠帝室之瑰寶，清廟之偉器。

translations.literal: Dangling tassels jade steps—discourse Way purple palace—truly imperial house's rare treasure—pure temple's great vessel.
translations.idiomatic: let tassels brush the jade stairs while he teaches in the purple palace—he would be the throne's jewel and the ancestral shrine's great vessel.

sentences.zh: 廣樂九奏，必登昊天之庭；

translations.literal: Great music nine performances—must ascend bright Heaven's court;
translations.idiomatic: Grand music played ninefold belongs in heaven's hall;

sentences.zh: 《韶》《夏》六變，必饗上帝之祀矣。

translations.literal: Shao and Xia six transformations—must feast High God's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: the Shao and Xia suites in six turns belong at High God's altar."

sentences.zh: 入為尚書郎、侍御史、太子中舍人、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Entered as Palace Writer gentleman—attending censor—Crown Palace attendant—Secretariat vice-president.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace writer, attendant censor, crown prince attendant, and vice-president of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎表為清河內史。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Ying memorialized him Plain Interior Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chengdu recommended him interior secretary of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 穎將討齊王冏，以雲為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: Ying about to punish Prince Qi Jiong—used Yun as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying marched against Prince Jiong of Qi he named Lu Yun vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 會冏誅，轉大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: When Jiong executed—transferred Grand General right major.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell he became senior major on the grand general's right.

sentences.zh: 穎晚節政衰，雲屢以正言忤旨。

translations.literal: Ying late stage governance declined—Yun repeatedly by straight speech offended intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's rule rotted in his later years—Lu Yun's blunt counsel repeatedly angered him.

sentences.zh: 孟玖欲用其父為邯鄲令，左長史盧志等並阿意從之，而雲固執不許，曰：「此縣皆公府掾資，豈有黃門父居之邪！

translations.literal: Meng Jiu wished employ his father as Handan county magistrate—left chief clerk Lu Zhi and others together flattered intent followed—yet Yun firmly held not permitted—saying: "This county all public office aide qualifications—how can yellow gate father dwell there!
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu wanted his father named magistrate of Handan; Lu Zhi and others humored him—Lu Yun refused: "That post belongs to tested aides—how can a eunuch's father hold it?"

sentences.zh: 」玖深忿怨。

translations.literal: Jiu deeply resentful hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 張昌為亂，穎上雲為使持節、大都督、前鋒將軍以討昌。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang made rebellion—Ying memorialized Yun as commissioner with credentials, grand commander, vanguard general to punish Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rose, Prince Ying named Lu Yun commissioner, commander-in-chief, and vanguard against him.

sentences.zh: 會伐長沙王，乃止。

translations.literal: When about to attack Prince Changsha—thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against Prince Yi of Changsha canceled that order.

sentences.zh: 機之敗也，並收雲。

translations.literal: When Ji met defeat—together seized Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's defeat led to Lu Yun's arrest.

sentences.zh: 穎官屬江統、蔡克、棗嵩等上疏曰：

translations.literal: Ying's official staff Jiang Tong, Cai Ke, Zao Song and others submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers Jiang Tong, Cai Ke, Zao Song, and others petitioned Prince Ying:

sentences.zh: 統等聞人主聖明，臣下盡規，苟有所懷，不敢不獻。

translations.literal: We hear when lord sage bright—ministers below exhaust regulation—if have what cherish—dare not fail present.
translations.idiomatic: When a lord is wise, ministers speak plainly—we dare hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 昨聞教以陸機後失軍期，師徒敗績，以法加刑，莫不謂當。

translations.literal: Yesterday heard instruction—that Lu Ji afterward missed army deadline—army-host routed—by law added punishment—none did not say fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's report said Lu Ji missed his rendezvous and his army broke—the law calls for punishment and none deny it.

sentences.zh: 誠足以肅齊三軍，威示遠近，所謂一人受戮，天下知誡者也。

translations.literal: Truly sufficient to solemnize three armies—awe display far near—so-called one man receives execution—world knows warning.
translations.idiomatic: Execution would stiffen the host and warn the realm—one death teaching every quarter.

sentences.zh: 且聞重教，以機圖為反逆，應加族誅，未知本末者，莫不疑惑。

translations.literal: Moreover heard heavy instruction—that Ji pictured as rebellious—should add clan execute—those who know not root tip—none not doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet graver word brands Lu Ji traitor and demands his clan—those who lack facts stand baffled.

sentences.zh: 夫爵人於朝，與眾共之；

translations.literal: Now ennobling men at court—together crowd shares them;
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing rank belongs to the court with all the world watching;

sentences.zh: 刑人於市，與眾棄之。

translations.literal: executing men at market—together crowd abandons them.
translations.idiomatic: inflicting death belongs to the marketplace with all the world judging.

sentences.zh: 惟刑之恤，古人所慎。

translations.literal: Only punishment's pity—ancients cautioned.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy in punishment was every sage's care.

sentences.zh: 今明公興舉義兵，以除國難，四海同心，雲合回應，罪人之命，懸於漏刻，泰平之期，不旦則夕矣。

translations.literal: Now enlightened lord raises righteous armies—to remove state calamity—four seas same heart—cloud join echo respond—criminal men's lives—hang on clepsydra—great peace's term—not dawn then evening.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness raises the righteous host to save the state—the empire rallies—traitors' breath runs out—peace comes within hours.

sentences.zh: 機兄弟並蒙拔擢，俱受重任，不當背罔極之恩，而向垂亡之寇；

translations.literal: Ji brothers together received promotion—together received heavy duty—should not betray endless grace—yet face dying bandit;
translations.idiomatic: The Lu brothers owed you preferment and heavy trust—they could hardly repay endless kindness by siding with a doomed foe—

sentences.zh: 去泰山之安，而赴累卵之危也。

translations.literal: leave Mount Tai's peace—yet rush piled-egg peril.
translations.idiomatic: to flee Taishan's safety for an egg-shell gamble.

sentences.zh: 直以機計慮淺近，不能董攝群帥，致果殺敵，進退之間，事有疑似，故令聖鑒未察其實耳。

translations.literal: Straight because Ji's planning shallow near—unable supervise gather commanders—achieve fruit kill enemy—advance retreat between—affairs had suspicion likeness—therefore made sagely mirror not inspect its reality.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji erred from shallow counsel—he could not bind his generals or crush the foe—his moves seemed dubious but that proves no rebellion.

sentences.zh: 刑誅事大，言機有反逆之征，宜令王粹、牽秀檢校其事。

translations.literal: Punishment execution affair great—speaking Ji has rebellion trace—should order Wang Cui, Qian Xiu inspect verify its affair.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guilt demands proof—if Lu Ji rebelled, let Wang Cui and Qian Xiu investigate.

sentences.zh: 令事驗顯然，暴之萬姓，然後加雲等之誅，未足為晚。

translations.literal: Order affair verification manifest—expose to myriad surnames—then afterward add Yun and others' execution—not sufficient as late.
translations.idiomatic: Let facts face the people—then execute Lu Yun and kin—still not too late.

sentences.zh: 今此舉措，實為太重，得則足令天下情服，失則必使四方心離，不可不令審諦，不可不令詳慎。

translations.literal: Now this measure—actually as too heavy—gain then sufficient order world sentiment submit—lose then must make four quarters heart depart—cannot not order careful examine—cannot not order detailed cautious.
translations.idiomatic: This stroke is too harsh—success wins hearts; failure splits the empire—we beg deliberate care.

sentences.zh: 統等區區，非為陸雲請一身之命，實慮此舉有得失之機，敢竭愚戇，以備誹謗。

translations.literal: Tong and others petty—not for Lu Yun ask one body's life—actually worry this measure has gain-loss pivot—dare exhaust foolish blunt—to prepare slander.
translations.idiomatic: We plead not for Lu Yun alone—we fear how this deed tips fortune—so we speak bluntly though it risks blame.

sentences.zh: 穎不納。

translations.literal: Ying did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 統等重請，穎遲回者三日。

translations.literal: Tong and others repeated request—Ying delayed circling three days.
translations.idiomatic: They petitioned again; Prince Ying hesitated three days.

sentences.zh: 盧志又曰：「昔趙王殺中護軍趙浚，赦其子驤，驤詣明公而擊趙，即前事也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi again said: "Formerly Prince Zhao killed Palace Guard Commander Zhao Jun—pardoned his son Xiang—Xiang visited enlightened lord then struck Zhao—that former affair."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi cited Prince Lun executing Zhao Jun yet sparing Zhao Xiang who later attacked Lun—a precedent for mercy.

sentences.zh: 」蔡克入至穎前，叩頭流血，曰：「雲為孟玖所怨，遠近莫不聞。

translations.literal: Cai Ke entered arrived Ying before—knocked head bleeding—saying: "Yun by Meng Jiu resented—far near none not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ke rushed to Prince Ying and knocked his brow bloody: "Everyone knows Meng Jiu hates Lu Yun."

sentences.zh: 今果見殺，罪無彰驗，將令群心疑惑，竊為明公惜之。

translations.literal: Now indeed seen killed—crime without manifest verification—will order crowd hearts doubtful—privately for enlightened lord pity it.
translations.idiomatic: Now Lu Yun dies without proof—the realm will doubt—your servant grieves for Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」僚屬隨克入者數十人，流涕固請，穎惻然有宥雲色。

translations.literal: Staff followers following Ke entered—several tens—tear flow firmly request—Ying saddened had pardon Yun color.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of aides followed, weeping and begging—Prince Ying softened toward sparing Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 孟玖扶穎入，催令殺雲。

translations.literal: Meng Jiu supported Ying enter—urged order kill Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu hustled Prince Ying inside and pressed him to kill Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 時年四十二。

translations.literal: Then age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun was forty-two.

sentences.zh: 有二女，無男。

translations.literal: Had two daughters—no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left two daughters and no son.

sentences.zh: 門生故吏迎喪葬清河，修墓立碑，四時祠祭。

translations.literal: Disciples old clerks welcomed mourning bury Qinghe—repair tomb erect stele—four seasons sacrifice offer.
translations.idiomatic: Students and former aides bore him to Qinghe, built his tomb and stele, and sacrifice each season.

sentences.zh: 所著文章三百四十九篇，又撰《新書》十篇，並行於世。

translations.literal: Composed writings three hundred forty-nine pieces—again composed New Writings ten pieces—all circulated in age.
translations.idiomatic: His writings numbered 349 pieces plus ten chapters of New Writings—all widely read.

sentences.zh: 初，雲嘗行，逗宿故人家，夜暗迷路，莫知所從。

translations.literal: Formerly Yun once traveled—stopped lodge old friend's house—night dark lost road—not knew what follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun once lodged with an old friend, lost his way in darkness, and knew not which path to take.

sentences.zh: 忽望草中有火光，於是趣之。

translations.literal: Suddenly saw grass inside had fire light—thereupon hurried it.
translations.idiomatic: He saw a glow in the grass and hurried toward it.

sentences.zh: 至一家，便寄宿，見一年少，美風姿，共談老子，辭致深遠。

translations.literal: Arrived one house—then lodged overnight—saw one young—beautiful bearing—together discussed Laozi—phrasing reached deep far.
translations.idiomatic: He reached a house and stayed—met a handsome youth—they debated the Laozi with penetrating wit.

sentences.zh: 向曉辭去，行十許裏，至故人家，雲此數十里中無人居，雲意始悟。

translations.literal: Toward dawn bid leave—walked ten-some li—arrived old friend's house—said this several tens li inside no men dwell—Yun intent began awaken.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he left; ten li on he reached his friend's house and learned no one lived for miles—then grasped the strangeness.

sentences.zh: 卻尋昨宿處，乃王弼塚。

translations.literal: Turned sought yesterday lodge place—actually Wang Bi mound.
translations.idiomatic: Searching back for last night's inn, he found Wang Bi's tomb.

sentences.zh: 雲本無玄學，自此談老殊進。

translations.literal: Yun originally lacked arcane learning—from this discuss Laozi greatly advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun had ignored metaphysics—after that night his discourse on the Laozi leaped forward.

sentences.zh: 雲弟耽

translations.literal: Yun younger brother Dan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan

sentences.zh: 雲弟耽為平東祭酒，亦有清譽，與雲同遇害。

translations.literal: Yun younger brother Dan became Pingdong libationer—also had pure reputation—with Yun together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Lu Dan served as libationer to the general pacifying the east, enjoyed a clean name, and died with Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 大將軍參軍孫惠與淮南內史硃誕書曰：「不意三陸相攜暗朝，一旦湮滅，道業淪喪，痛酷之深，荼毒難言。

translations.literal: Grand General aide Sun Hui wrote letter to Huainan Interior Secretary Zhu Dan saying: "Did not expect Three Lu mutually carried dark court—once sank extinct—Way enterprise sunk lost—pain cruel deep—bitter poison hard speak.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui wrote Zhu Dan, "The Three Lus vanished together into a blind court—their teaching lost—grief cuts deeper than words."

sentences.zh: 國喪俊望，悲豈一人！

translations.literal: State lost handsome outlook—grief could only one person!
translations.idiomatic: The realm lost its brightest—not one man's sorrow!"

sentences.zh: 」其為州裏所痛悼如此。

translations.literal: Such local districts mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Their district mourned them so.

sentences.zh: 後東海王越討穎，移檄天下，亦以機、雲兄弟枉害罪狀穎雲。

translations.literal: Later Prince Donghai Yue punished Ying—moved proclamation world—also by Ji, Yun brothers wrongful harm charged Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Yue of Donghai attacked Prince Ying and cited the wrongful deaths of the Lu brothers among his crimes.

sentences.zh: 從叔喜

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Xi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi

sentences.zh: 喜字恭仲。

translations.literal: Xi courtesy Gongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi, courtesy Gongzhong.

sentences.zh: 父瑁，吳吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Father Mao—Wu Ministry of Personnel Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Mao had been Wu's minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 喜仕吳，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xi served Wu—successively rose Ministry of Personnel Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi served Wu and rose to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 少有聲名，好學有才思。

translations.literal: Youth had fame reputation—loved learning had talent thought.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned as a youth, he loved study and showed literary wit.

sentences.zh: 嘗為自敘，其略曰：「劉向省《新語》而作《新序》，桓譚詠《新序》而作《新論》。

translations.literal: Once composed self-account—its outline said: "Liu Xiang examined New Conversations then composed New Sequence—Huan Tan chanted New Sequence then composed New Discourse."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote an autobiographical sketch: "Liu Xiang condensed the New Conversations into the New Prefaces; Huan Tan responded with the New Discourse."

sentences.zh: 餘不自量，感子雲之《法言》而作《言道》，睹賈子之美才而作《訪論》，觀子政《洪範》而作《古今曆》，鑒蔣子通《萬機》而作《審機》，讀《幽通》、《思玄》、《四愁》而作《娛賓》、《九思》，真所謂忍愧者也。

translations.literal: I not self-measure—moved by Ziyun's Model Sayings then composed Speak on the Way—saw Jiazi's fine talent then composed Inquiry Discussion—viewed Zizheng's Great Plan then composed Ancient-Modern Calendar—mirrored Jiang Zitong's Myriad Matters then composed Examining Matters—read You Tong, Si Xuan, Four Sorrows then composed Guest's Delight, Nine Thoughts—truly so-called endure shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shamelessly stirred by Yang Xiong's Model Words I wrote On the Way; admiring Jia Yi I wrote an Inquiry; studying Liu Xiang's Great Plan I compiled calendars ancient and modern; reviewing Jiang Yong's myriad affairs I wrote Scrutinizing Affairs; reading Ban's laments I penned Guest's Delight and Nine Thoughts—pure vanity."

sentences.zh: 」其書近百篇。

translations.literal: His writings nearly hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His books approached one hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 吳平，又作《西州清論》傳於世，借稱諸葛孔明以行其書也。

translations.literal: Wu pacified—again composed Western Province Pure Discussion circulated in age—borrow styled Zhuge Kongming to circulate his book.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he issued Western Province Pure Discussion under Zhuge Liang's name to gain readers.

sentences.zh: 有《較論格品篇》曰：

translations.literal: Had Compare Discuss Rank Types chapter saying:
translations.idiomatic: His chapter Ranking Worthies runs:

sentences.zh: 或問予，薛瑩最是國士之第一者乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked me—is Xue Ying foremost state's knight first?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked whether Xue Ying ranked first among Wu worthies.

sentences.zh: 答曰：'以理推之，在乎四五之間，問者愕然請問。

translations.literal: Answered saying: 'By principle infer—it lies between fourth fifth—questioner stunned requested ask.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Judging coolly, he sits fourth or fifth—the listener gaped and pressed him."

sentences.zh: 答曰：'夫孫皓無道，肆其暴虐，若龍蛇其身，沈默其體，潛而勿用，趣不可測，此第一人也。

translations.literal: Answered saying: 'Now Sun Hao lacked Way—unleash his violent cruelty—like dragon snake its body—silent its form—hidden yet not use—trend cannot measure—this first man.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: amid Sun Hao's tyranny the man who coils like a dragon, stays silent, hides unused—trackless danger.

sentences.zh: 避尊居卑，祿代耕養，玄靜守約，沖退澹然，此第二人也。

translations.literal: Avoid honor dwell low—salary replaces plow nurture—dark quiet keep restraint—surge retreat tranquil—this second man.
translations.idiomatic: Second: avoiding rank for humble pay, farming rice in quiet seclusion.

sentences.zh: 侃然體國思治，心不辭貴，以方見憚，執政不懼，此第三人也。

translations.literal: Straight body state's thinking rule—heart not decline noble—by square seen fear—holding governance not fear—this third man.
translations.idiomatic: Third: candor for the state despite perilous office.

sentences.zh: 斟酌時宜，在亂猶顯，意不忘忠，時獻微益，此第四人也。

translations.literal: Deliberate weigh timely fit—in chaos still manifest—intent not forget loyalty—times present slight benefit—this fourth man.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: weighing each hour, loyal even in chaos, offering modest good.

sentences.zh: 溫恭修慎，不為諂首，無所雲補，從容保寵，此第五人也。

translations.literal: Warm respectful cultivate cautious—not become flattery head—nothing cloud supplement—follow ease preserve favor—this fifth man.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: mild, careful, never leading flatterers—harmless yet keeping favor.

sentences.zh: 過此已往，不足復數。

translations.literal: Pass this gone forward—not worth again count.
translations.idiomatic: Below these none merit counting.

sentences.zh: 故第二已上，多淪沒而遠悔吝，第三已下，有聲位而近咎累。

translations.literal: Therefore second already above—many sink drowned yet far regret shame—third already below—have sound position yet near fault accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Above the second many vanished shy of scandal; below the third fame brought blame.

sentences.zh: 是以深識君子，晦其明而履柔順也。

translations.literal: Therefore deep-knowing gentlemen—dim their brightness yet tread gentle yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Wise men therefore veil brilliance and stay supple.

sentences.zh: '問者曰：'始聞高論，終年啟寤矣。'

translations.literal: Questioner said: 'Beginning heard high discourse—whole year awakened.'
translations.idiomatic: The questioner said, "Your words wake me after a year of sleep."

sentences.zh: 太康中，下詔曰：「偽尚書陸喜等十五人，南士歸稱，並以貞潔不容皓朝，或忠而獲罪，或退身修志，放在草野。

translations.literal: Taikang middle—issued edict saying: "False Wu Minister Lu Xi and others fifteen men—southern gentlemen returned praised—all by chaste pure not tolerated Hao court—or loyal yet got crime—or retreat body cultivate will—release among grass wild.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Taikang edict: fifteen Wu ministers including Lu Xi—Southerners praised—were too honest for Sun Hao or loyal yet punished or withdrew to the wild.

sentences.zh: 主者可皆隨本位就下拜除，敕所在以禮發遣，須到隨才授用。

translations.literal: Responsible ones may all follow original rank descend appoint—order regions by ritual dispatch send—must arrive follow talent grant use.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities shall reinstate their offices by courtesy and assign posts by talent.

sentences.zh: 」乃以喜為散騎常侍，尋卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon appointed Xi Cavalier Attendant Regular—soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi became palace attendant and soon died.

sentences.zh: 子育，為尚書郎、弋陽太守。

translations.literal: Son Yu—became Palace Writer gentleman—Yiyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Yu served as palace writer and prefect of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：古人云：「雖楚有才，晉實用之。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: ancients said: "Although Chu has talent—Jin truly uses it."
translations.idiomatic: The historian's verdict: "Chu may breed talent; Jin in the end employed it."

sentences.zh: 」觀夫陸機、陸雲，實荊、衡之杞梓，挺圭璋於秀實，馳英華於早年，風鑒澄爽，神情俊邁。

translations.literal: Gazing on Lu Ji, Lu Yun—truly Jing, Heng's catalpa—straight jade in splendid fruit—gallop flower brilliance in early years—wind mirror clear bright—spirit mien handsome distant.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji and Lu Yun were the finest timber of Jing and Heng—jade in the bud, splendor in youth, judgment limpid, spirit bold.

sentences.zh: 文藻宏麗，獨步當時；

translations.literal: Writing carving vast splendid—sole walk current age;
translations.idiomatic: Their prose outshone the age;

sentences.zh: 言論慷慨，冠乎終古。

translations.literal: speech discussion generous ardent—crown over end-to-ancient.
translations.idiomatic: their words rang loftier than antiquity's best.

sentences.zh: 高詞迥映，如朗月之懸光；

translations.literal: High phrases far reflect—like bright moon's hanging light;
translations.idiomatic: Soaring lines gleam like a clear moon;

sentences.zh: 疊意回舒，若重岩之積秀。

translations.literal: stacked meaning return expand—like layered crags' piled splendor.
translations.idiomatic: layered thought rolls like misted peaks.

sentences.zh: 千條析理，則電坼霜開；

translations.literal: Thousand strands analyze principle—then lightning split frost open;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand arguments crack like lightning on frost;

sentences.zh: 一緒連文，則珠流璧合。

translations.literal: one thread link writing—then pearl flow jade join.
translations.idiomatic: one theme knits jade to pearl.

sentences.zh: 其詞深而雅，其義博而顯，故足遠超枚、馬，高躡王、劉，百代文宗，一人而已。

translations.literal: Their phrasing deep yet elegant—their meaning broad yet manifest—therefore sufficient far surpass Mei, Ma—high tread Wang, Liu—hundred generations' writing patriarch—one man only.
translations.idiomatic: Depth and grace, reach and clarity—they surpass Mei and Sima, stride past Wang and Liu, and stand as the age's one literary patriarch.

sentences.zh: 然其祖考重光，羽楫吳運，文武奕葉，將相連華。

translations.literal: Yet their grandfather father double light—oars move Wu fortune—civil-military many leaves—generals ministers linked splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Forebears twinned eminence, oared Wu's fate, stacked civil and martial glory in unbroken offices.

sentences.zh: 而機以廊廟蘊才，瑚璉標器，宜其承俊乂之慶，奉佐時之業，申能展用，保譽流功。

translations.literal: Yet Ji with hall-temple store talent—coral jade mark vessel—should that inherit outstanding ones' blessing—uphold assist-age enterprise—extend ability deploy use—preserve reputation flow merit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji bore hall-and-temple gifts, shone like ritual jade—fit to claim wise men's blessing, aid the hour, and leave lasting praise.

sentences.zh: 屬吳祚傾基，金陵畢氣，君移國滅，家喪臣遷。

translations.literal: Attaching Wu fate tilted base—Jinling exhausts breath—lord moved state perish—house lost minister shift.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu's pillar cracked, Jinling's breath failed, the ruler fell, the state perished, families scattered.

sentences.zh: 矯翮南辭，翻棲火樹；

translations.literal: Straighten wing south bid—turn roost fire tree;
translations.idiomatic: They straightened wings to leave the south and roosted in a burning tree;

sentences.zh: 飛鱗北逝，卒委湯池。

translations.literal: flying scales north depart—finally entrust boiling pool.
translations.idiomatic: they flicked northward scales and sank into scalding pools.

sentences.zh: 遂使穴碎雙龍，巢傾兩鳳。

translations.literal: Thereupon made cave shatter twin dragons—nest tilt two phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Their lair shattered two dragons; their nest toppled twin phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 激浪之心未騁，遽骨修鱗；

translations.literal: Surge wave heart not gallop—suddenly bones long scales;
translations.idiomatic: Surge-tossed hearts never raced—long fins turned bare bones;

sentences.zh: 陵雲之意將騰，先灰勁翮。

translations.literal: cloud-top intent about soar—first ash strong pinions.
translations.idiomatic: cloud-soaring will barely stirred—strong pinions burned first.

sentences.zh: 望其翔躍，焉可得哉！

translations.literal: Hope their soar leap—how can obtain!
translations.idiomatic: Who could watch them soar again?

sentences.zh: 夫賢之立身，以功名為本；

translations.literal: Now worthy's establishing body—by merit fame as root;
translations.idiomatic: The worthy stake life on merit and name;

sentences.zh: 士之居世，以富貴為先。

translations.literal: knight's dwelling age—by wealth honor first.
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen face the world seeking fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 然則榮利人之所貪，禍辱人之所惡，故居安保名，則君子處焉；

translations.literal: Being thus glory profit men's what greedy—calamity shame men's what hate—therefore dwell peace preserve name—then gentleman dwells;
translations.idiomatic: Glory lures and ruin terrifies—so gentlemen nest where safety guards reputation;

sentences.zh: 冒危履貴，則哲士去焉。

translations.literal: risk danger tread honor—then wise man departs.
translations.idiomatic: sages flee when danger buys rank.

sentences.zh: 是知蘭植中塗，必無經時之翠；

translations.literal: This knows orchid plant middle ford—must lack enduring-time's green;
translations.idiomatic: Orchids planted mid-road cannot stay green;

sentences.zh: 桂生幽壑，終保彌年之丹。

translations.literal: cassia born hidden gorge—end preserves filling-years' cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: cassia rooted in deep valleys keeps red fragrance years.

sentences.zh: 非蘭怨而桂親，豈塗害而壑利？

translations.literal: Not orchid resents yet cassia intimate—could ford harm yet gorge profit?
translations.idiomatic: Not because orchids hate cassias—exposure harms, shelter profits.

sentences.zh: 而生滅有殊者，隱顯之勢異也。

translations.literal: Yet birth extinction has difference—hidden manifest momentum differs.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death diverge by hidden or exposed.

sentences.zh: 故曰，衒美非所，罕有常安；

translations.literal: Therefore says—display beauty not place—rarely has constant peace;
translations.idiomatic: Thus flashing greatness out of place seldom stays safe;

sentences.zh: 韜奇擇居，故能全性。

translations.literal: hide wonder choose dwelling—therefore can preserve nature.
translations.idiomatic: treasuring odd gifts in wise recess preserves one's nature.

sentences.zh: 觀機、雲之行己也，智不逮言矣。

translations.literal: Observe Ji, Yun's conduct self—wisdom not reach speech.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Lu Ji and Lu Yun lived—wit fell short of their words.

sentences.zh: 睹其文章之誡，何知易而行難？

translations.literal: See their essays' warnings—how know easy yet practice hard?
translations.idiomatic: Their essays preach caution—why easier read than done?

sentences.zh: 自以智足安時，才堪佐命，庶保名位，無忝前基。

translations.literal: Self-thought wisdom sufficient pacify age—talent worth aid mandate—hope preserve name rank—not shame former foundation.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted mind enough for the times and talent fit to aid Heaven—hoping to save name and honor forbears.

sentences.zh: 不知世屬未通，運鐘方否，進不能辟昏匡亂，退不能屏跡全身，而奮力危邦，竭心庸主，忠抱實而不諒，謗緣虛而見疑，生在己而難長，死因人而易促。

translations.literal: Not know generation fate not open—fortune bell just obstruct—advance cannot dispel dark rectify chaos—retreat cannot screen traces preserve body—yet rouse strength peril state—exhaust heart mediocre lord—loyalty embrace solid yet not trusted—slander edge empty yet seen suspect—life in self yet hard long—death because person yet easy hasten.
translations.idiomatic: They missed Heaven's closed gate while fortune tolled ill—could not cleanse darkness or hide safely—yet strained in perilous courts for mediocre lords; loyalty went unbelieved, idle slander drew suspicion; life stayed fragile, death came swift.

sentences.zh: 上蔡之犬，不誡于前，華亭之鶴，方悔於後。

translations.literal: Shangcai's dogs—not warned before—Huating's cranes—only regret after.
translations.idiomatic: They never heeded the hunting dogs at Shangcai until Huating's cranes taught regret too late.

sentences.zh: 卒令覆宗絕祀，良可悲夫！

translations.literal: Finally ordered overturn clan cut sacrifice—truly can be mourned!
translations.idiomatic: Their house fell and their ancestral offerings ceased—how bitter a fate!

sentences.zh: 然則三世為將，釁鐘來葉；

translations.literal: Being thus three generations as generals—calamity bell comes to posterity;
translations.idiomatic: Three generations under arms invite Heaven's bell—and later leaves bear the wound;

sentences.zh: 誅降不祥，殃及後昆。

translations.literal: Executing surrender not auspicious—calamity reaches posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Slaying those who yield courts ill luck—and children's children pay the price.

sentences.zh: 是知西陵結其凶端，河橋收其禍末，其天意也，豈人事乎！

translations.literal: This knows Xiling tied its vicious beginning—River Bridge gathered its calamity end—its Heaven's intent—could human affairs!
translations.idiomatic: So Xiling seeded their doom and the Yellow River bridge sealed it—was that Heaven's ledger, not mortal deed?
